& & {\ensuremath{T_{\rm fp}}} \Phi \ar[r]^-{\sim} & \mathop{\rm{term}} \Phi \\
& {\ensuremath{T_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[r]^-{\sim} \ar[ur]_{\eta}
& \{\mbox{\rm linear $\Phi$-terms}\} \ar@{^{((}->}[ur]
}
\]
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By definition, the presentation is linear iff $\pi_1, \pi_2$ factor
through the signature of linear $\Phi$-terms.
By Lemma \ref{lem:syntactic_semantic_equiv}, this signature is isomorphic to
${\ensuremath{T_{\Sigma}}} \Phi$, so we are done.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
Let $Q \in {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{FP-Operad}}}}}$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Q$ is strongly regular iff there exists a $P \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Operad}}}}$ such that $Q \cong {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\rm pl}}} P$;
\item $Q$ is linear iff there exists a $P \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$ such that $Q \cong
{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}} P$;
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We will consider the linear case; the strongly regular case is proved
analogously.

If $Q$ is linear, then there exists a linear presentation $ \xymatrix{E \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{} & {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}} \Phi} $ for $Q$.
We may regard $E$ as a subobject of the signature of $\Phi$-equations.
By assumption, $E$ consists only of linear equations; by Lemma
\ref{lem:syntactic_semantic_equiv}, every $(s,t) \in E$ is $(\mathop{\rm{term}}(\sigma_1
\cdot \tau_1), \mathop{\rm{term}}(\sigma_2 \cdot \tau_2))$ for some pair $(\sigma_1 \cdot
\tau_1, \sigma_2 \cdot \tau_2)$ of permuted trees.
So the diagram $ \xymatrix{E \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{} & {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}} \Phi} $ in {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{FP-Operad}}}}}\ is the image
under ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ of a diagram
\[
 \xymatrix{E' \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{} & {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi} 
\]
in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$.
This diagram has a coequalizer: call it $P$.
The functor ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ is a left adjoint, and thus preserves coequalizers:
hence, $Q$ is the image under ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ of $P$.

Now suppose $Q = {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}} P$ for some symmetric operad $P$.
We may take the canonical presentation of $P$:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}

	\xymatrix{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{\epsilon{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon} & {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^-{\epsilon} & P }

\]
and apply ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ to it:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}

	\xymatrix{{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}}({\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P) \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon} & {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^-{{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon} & {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}} P = Q }

\]
Since ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ is a left adjoint, it preserves coequalizers, so the transpose
of this parallel pair is a presentation for $Q$.
Take this transpose:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P
	\ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{\overline{\epsilon{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}}} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{\overline{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon}}
	& {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^{\eta'}
	& {{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P} \ar[r]^{{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}}{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}\epsilon}
	& {\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} Q
}
\]
where $\eta'$ is the unit of the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}}$, and the bars
refer to transposition with respect to the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}$.

This is in precisely the form required for Lemma \ref{lem:linpresfactor}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- example-14: body_md -->
\index{monoids}
\index{pointed sets}
\index{commutative monoids}
The theories of monoids and pointed sets are strongly regular, because the finite product operads\ corresponding to these theories are in the image of ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\rm pl}}}$; the theory of
commutative monoids is linear but not strongly regular, because the finite product operad\ whose
algebras are commutative monoids is in the image of ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}$ but not in the
image of ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\rm pl}}}$.
<!-- end example-14 -->
<!-- defn-54: body_md -->
\index{wide pullback}
A \textbf{wide pullback} is a limit of a (possibly infinite) diagram of the
form
\[
\xymatrixrowsep{1pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	\bullet \ar[ddr] \\
	\bullet \ar[dr] \\
	\vdots & \bullet \\
	\bullet \ar[ur] \\
	\vdots
}
\]
<!-- end defn-54 -->
<!-- defn-55: body_md -->
\index{cartesian!natural transformation}
A natural transformation $\alpha : F \to G$ is \textbf{cartesian} if every
naturality square
\[

	\xymatrix{
		FA \ar[r]^-{Ff} \ar[d]_-{\alpha_A}
		& FB \ar[d]^-{\alpha_B} \\
		GA \ar[r]^-{Gf}
		& GB
	}

\]
is a pullback square.
<!-- end defn-55 -->
<!-- defn-56: body_md -->
\index{cartesian!monad}
A monad $(T, \mu, \eta)$ is \textbf{cartesian} if $T$ preserves pullbacks and
$\mu, \eta$ are cartesian natural transformations.
<!-- end defn-56 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:opds<=>cart. monad}
A plain operad is equivalent to a cartesian monad on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}\ equipped with a
cartesian map of monads to the free monoid monad.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
See \cite{hohc} 6.2.4.
Let 1 be the terminal plain operad; algebras for 1 are monoids.
Since 1 is terminal, every plain operad $P$ comes equipped with a map $!: P \to
1$.
This induces a cartesian map of monads $T_! : T_P \to T_1$, and $T_1$ is the
free monoid monad.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
Let $T, S$ be endofunctors on a category $\Acat$, let $\alpha : T \to S$ be a
cartesian natural transformation, and let $S$ preserve wide pullbacks.
Then $T$ preserves wide pullbacks.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
This follows from the facts that wide pullbacks are products in slice
categories and that the functor $f^* : \Acat/B \to \Acat/A$ induced by a map $f
: A \to B$ is product-preserving.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:wpb}
Let $P$ be a plain operad.
Then the functor part of the  monad $T_P$ arising from $P$ preserves wide
pullbacks.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- defn-57: body_md -->
\index{familial representability}
A functor $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$ is \textbf{familially representable} if $F$ is a
coproduct of representable functors.
A monad $(T, \mu, \eta)$ on $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$ is \textbf{familially representable} if $T$
is familially representable.
<!-- end defn-57 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
(Carboni-Johnstone)
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ be a complete, locally small, well-powered category with a small
cogenerating set, and let $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$ be a functor.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is familially representable;
\item $F$ preserves wide pullbacks.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
See \cite{c+j1}, Theorem 2.6.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
The monad associated to a strongly regular theory is familially representable.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- defn-58: body_md -->
\index{involutive monoid}
\index{monoid with involution|see{involutive monoid}}
An \textbf{involutive monoid} (or \textbf{monoid with involution}) is a
monoid $(M,.,1)$ equipped with an involution $i : M \to M$,
satisfying $i(a.b) = i(b).i(a)$.
<!-- end defn-58 -->
<!-- defn-59: body_md -->
\index{multicategory!plain!enriched}
A \textbf{$\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}$-multicategory} $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ consists of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item a collection $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}_0$ of \emph{objects},
\item for all $n \in \natural$ and all $c_1, \dots, c_n,
d \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}_0$, an object $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_1, \dots, c_n; d) \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}$ called the
\emph{arrows} from $c_1, \dots, c_n$ to $d$,
\item for all $n, k_1, \dots k_n \in \natural$ and $c_1^1 \dots, c_{k_n}^n,
d_1, \dots, d_n, e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}_0$, an arrow in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}$ called \emph{composition}
\[\circ
: \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(d_1, \dots, d_n;e)  \otimes
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c^1_1, \dots, c^1_{k_1};d_1) \otimes \dots \otimes
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c^n_1, \dots, c^n_{k_n};d_n)
\to
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c^1_1, \dots, c^n_{k_n};e)\]
\item for all $c \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, a \emph{unit} $u_c: I \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c;c)$
\end{itemize}
satisfying the following axioms:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Associativity:} For all $b^\bullet_{\bullet\bullet}, c_\bullet^\bullet, d_\bullet, e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the
following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{1.5pc}
\xymatrix{
	*\txt{$\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(d_\bullet; e) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c^1_\bullet; d_1) \otimes \dots \otimes
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c^n_\bullet; d_n)$ \\
	$\otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^1_{1\bullet}; c^1_1) \otimes
	\dots \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^{n}_{k_n\bullet}; c^n_{k_n})$}
		\ar[r]^-\circ
		\ar[dd]^-\circ
		&
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(d_\bullet; e) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^1_{\bullet\bullet}; d_1) \otimes \dots \otimes
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^n_{\bullet\bullet}; d_n)
		\ar[dd]^-\circ
		\\ \\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet^\bullet; e) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^1_{1\bullet}; c^1_1) \otimes
	\dots \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^{n}_{k_n\bullet}; c^n_{k_n})
		\ar[r]^-\circ
		&
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b^\bullet_{\bullet\bullet} ; e)
}
\]
\item \emph{Units:} For all $c_\bullet, d \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{1.3pc}
\xymatrix{
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet ; d)
		 \ar[r]^\lambda
		 \ar[ddrr]^1
		 \ar[d]_{\rho^n}
		 &
	I \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet; d)
		\ar[dr]^{u \otimes 1}
		\\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet ; d) \otimes I \otimes \dots \otimes I
		\ar[dr]_{1\otimes u^{\otimes n}}
		&
		&
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(d;d) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet;d)
		\ar[d]^{\circ}
		\\
	&
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet ; d) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_1;c_1) \otimes \dots \otimes \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_n;c_n)
		\ar[r]^-{\circ}
		&
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(c_\bullet ; d)
}
\]
\end{itemize}
(We suppress the symmetry maps in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ for clarity).
<!-- end defn-59 -->
<!-- defn-60: body_md -->
\label{def:symmVmcat}
\index{multicategory!symmetric!enriched}
A \textbf{symmetric \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategory} is a \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategory \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ and, for every
$n \in \natural$, every $\sigma \in S_n$, and every $a_1, \dots a_n, b \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$,
an arrow
\[
\sigma \cdot - : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a_1, \dots, a_n; b) \longrightarrow 
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a_{\sigma 1}, \dots, a_{\sigma n}; b)
\]
in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item for each $n \in \natural$ and each $a_1, \dots, a_n, b \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the arrow
$1_n \cdot - : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a_1, \dots, a_n;b) \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a_1, \dots, a_n;b)$ is the identity
arrow on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a_1, \dots, a_n;b)$,
\item for each $\sigma, \rho \in S_n$,
\[
(\rho \cdot - )(\sigma \cdot -) = (\rho\sigma) \cdot -
\]
\item for each $n, k_1, \dots, k_n \in n$, each $\sigma \in S_n$ and $\rho_i
\in S_{k_i}$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$, and for all $a^1_1, \dots, a^n_{k_n}, b_1,
\dots, b_n, c \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the diagram
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{-5pc}
\xymatrix{
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b_1, \dots, b_n; c) \otimes \bigotimes_{i=1}^n{\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a^i_1,\dots, a^i_n; b_i)}
\ar[dl]_{(\sigma\cdot-) \otimes \bigotimes_{i=1}^n{(\rho_i\cdot -)}}
\ar[ddr]^\circ \\
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b_{\sigma 1}, \dots, b_{\sigma n};c)\otimes
	\bigotimes_{i=1}^n{\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a^i_{\rho_i 1}, \dots, a^i_{\rho_i n};b_i)}
\ar[dd]_{1\otimes \sigma_*} \\
& & \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a^1_1, \dots, a^n_{k_n}; c) \ar[ddl]^{\sigma \circ(\rho_1,\dots,\rho_n)}
\\
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(b_{\sigma 1}, \dots, b_{\sigma n};c) \otimes \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a^{\sigma
i}_{\rho_{\sigma i} 1}, \dots, a^{\sigma i}_{\rho_{\sigma i} n} ; b_{\sigma i})
\ar[dr]_\circ \\
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(a^{\sigma 1}_{\rho_{\sigma 1} 1}, \dots, a^{\sigma n}_{\rho_{\sigma n}
k_n}; c)
}
\]
commutes, where $\sigma\circ({\def\tmp#\rho_#1{\rho_#1} \tmp{1} , \dots , \tmp{n}})$ is as defined in Example
\ref{ex:symmopd}.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end defn-60 -->
<!-- defn-61: body_md -->
\index{multicategory!finite product!enriched}
A \textbf{finite product \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategory} is
\begin{itemize}
\item A plain \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategory \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}};
\item for every function $f : {\underline{n}} \to {\underline{m}}$ in \ensuremath{\bbF}, and for all objects $C_1,
\dots, C_n, D \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, a morphism $f\cdot - : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(C_1, \dots, C_n;D) \to
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(C_{f(1)}, \dots, C_{f(n)}; D)$ in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\,
\end{itemize}
satisfying the conditions given in Definition \ref{def:symmVmcat}, where
$(f\circ(f_1,\dots, f_n))$ is as given in Definition \ref{dopdef}.
<!-- end defn-61 -->
<!-- defn-62: body_md -->
\index{operad!enriched}
A (\textbf{plain}, \textbf{symmetric}, \textbf{finite product})
\textbf{\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-operad} is a (plain, symmetric, finite product) \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategory
with only one object.
<!-- end defn-62 -->
<!-- defn-63: body_md -->
\index{morphism!of enriched multicategories}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ be plain \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multicategories.
A \textbf{morphism} $F: \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ is
\begin{itemize}
\item for each object $C \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, a choice of object $FC \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$,
\item for each $n \in \natural$ and all collections of objects $A_1, \dots,
A_n, B \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, an arrow

$ \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(A_1, \dots, A_n;B) \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}(FA_1, \dots, FA_n; FB) $ in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}$
\end{itemize}
such that
\begin{itemize}
\item for all $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
 & I \ar[ddl]_u \ar[ddr]^u \\ \\
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(A;A) \ar[rr]^F & & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}(FA;FA)
}
\]
commutes;
\item for all $n, k_1, \dots, k_n \in \natural$ and all $C, B_1, \dots, B_n, A^1_1, \dots, A^n_{k_n} \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the diagram
\[
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(B_\bullet;C) \otimes \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(A^i_\bullet;B_i)
\ar[r]^-{\circ} \ar[d]_{F\otimes \dots \otimes F}
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}(A_\bullet^\bullet;C) \ar[d]^F \\
\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}(FB_\bullet;FC)\otimes \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}(F A^i_\bullet;FB_i)
\ar[r]^-\circ
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}(FA_\bullet^\bullet;FC)
}
\]
commutes.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end defn-63 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\index{multicategory!internal}
\index{operad!internal}
There is another possibility, that of considering \emph{internal}
multicategories in the category \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}, which gives a different notion: now
$\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}_0$ is an object in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ rather than a collection.
An internal operad in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ is an internal multicategory \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ such that $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}_0$ is
terminal in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}.
We shall not consider internal multicategories or operads further.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\index{operad!enriched!in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}}
A {(plain) \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad} $Q$ is a sequence of categories $Q_0, Q_1,
\dots$, a family of composition functors $\circ:Q_n \times Q_{k_1}
\times \ldots \times Q_{k_n} \to Q_{\sum k_i}$ and an identity 
$1_Q \in Q_1$, satisfying (strict) functorial versions of the axioms given in
\ref{lem:operad_description}.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
A {symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad} is a plain \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad $Q$ with a left group
action of each symmetric group $S_n$ on the corresponding category $Q_n$,
strictly satisfying equations as in Definition \ref{def:symmopd}.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
A {finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad} is a plain \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad $Q$ equipped with functors $f \cdot - :
Q_n \to Q_m$ for each function $f: {\underline{n}} \to {\underline{m}}$ of finite sets, strictly
satisfying equations as in Definition \ref{dopdef}.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- defn-64: body_md -->
\label{laxmorphdef}
\index{morphism!of algebras for a finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
Let $Q$ be a finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad, and let $Q \circ A \stackrel\alpha\to A , Q \circ B
\stackrel\beta\to B$ be algebras for $Q$ in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$. A
\textbf{lax morphism of $Q$-algebras} $A \to B$ consists of a 1-cell $F: A \to
B$ and a 2-cell $\phi: \beta F \to F \alpha$ satisfying the
following conditions:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:laxmorph1}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	A \ar[r]^F \ar[d]_\eta
	  \ddlowertwocell<-20>_1{=}                   
	  \drtwocell\omit{=}
	& B \ar[d]^\eta
	  \dduppertwocell<20>^1{=} \\                      
	Q\circ A \ar[r]^{1\circ F} \ar[d]_\alpha
	  \drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q\circ B \ar[d]^\beta
		& & = & A \rtwocell^F_F{=} & B \\
	A \ar[r]_F & B
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:laxmorph2}
\xymatrixcolsep{1.4pc}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q \circ Q \circ A \ar[d]_\mu \ar[r]^{1\circ 1\circ F}
	  \drtwocell\omit{=}
	& Q \circ Q \circ B \ar[d]^\mu
	& & & Q \circ Q \circ A \ar[dl]_\mu \ar[r]^{1\circ 1\circ F}
		\ar[d]_{1\circ \alpha}
		\drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q \circ Q \circ B  \ar[dr]^\mu \ar[d]^{1\circ \beta} \\
	Q \circ A \ar[r]^{1\circ F} \ar[d]_{\alpha}
		\drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q \circ B \ar[d]^{\beta}
	& =
	& Q \circ A \ar[dr]_{\alpha}
	  \rtwocell\omit{=}
	& Q \circ A \ar[r]^{1\circ F} \ar[d]_{\alpha}
		\drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q \circ B \ar[d]^{\beta}
	  \rtwocell\omit{=}
	& Q \circ B \ar[dl]^{\beta} \\
	A \ar[r]_F
	& B
	& & & A \ar[r]_F
	& B
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:laxmorph3}
\xymatrixcolsep{1.4pc}
\xymatrixnocompile{
	& Q_m \times A^n \ar[dl]_{1 \times f^*} \ar[dr]^{1 \times F^n}
		\ddtwocell\omit{=}
	& & & & Q_m \times A^n \ar[dl]_{1 \times f^*} \ar[dr]^{1 \times F^n}
		\ar[dd]^{f_* \times 1}
	\\
	        
	Q_m \times A^m \ar[dd]^\alpha \ar[dr]^{1 \times F^m}
	& & Q_m \times B^n \ar[dl]_{1 \times f^*} \ar[dd]^{f_* \times 1}
	& & Q_m \times A^m \ar[dd]^\alpha
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& & Q_m \times B^n \ar[dd]^{f_* \times 1} \\
	        
		\drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q_n \times B^m \ar[dd]^\beta
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& & =
	& & Q_n \times A^n \ar[dl]_\alpha \ar[dr]_{1 \times F^n}
		\urtwocell\omit{=}
		\ddtwocell\omit{\phi} \\
	        
	A \ar[dr]_F
	& & Q_n \times B^n \ar[dl]^\beta
	& & A \ar[dr]_F
	& & Q_n \times B^n \ar[dl]^\beta \\
	& B
	& & & & B
}
\end{equation}
for all functions $f : {\underline{m}} \to {\underline{n}}$.

A morphism $(F,\phi)$ is \textbf{weak} if $\phi$ is invertible, and
\textbf{strict} if $\phi$ is an identity.
\index{weak!morphism of algebras for a finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
\index{strict!morphism of algebras for a finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}

\index{morphism!of algebras for a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
\index{lax!morphism of algebras for a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
\index{weak!morphism of algebras for a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
\index{strict!morphism of algebras for a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
Lax morphisms for algebras of plain \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads are required to satisfy
\ref{eq:laxmorph1} and \ref{eq:laxmorph2}, and lax morphisms for algebras of
symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads are required to satisfy \ref{eq:laxmorph1},
\ref{eq:laxmorph2} and the restriction of \ref{eq:laxmorph3} to the case where
$f$ is a bijection.
<!-- end defn-64 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:wkfunc_explicit}
Let $Q$ be a plain $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$-operad, and let $(A,h)$ and $(B,h')$ be $Q$-algebras.
A lax map of $Q$-algebras $(A,h) \to (B,h')$ is a pair $(G, \psi)$,
where $G:A \to B$ is a functor and $\psi$ is a sequence of natural
transformations $\psi_i : h'_i (1 \times G^i) \to G h_i$, called the
\textbf{coherence maps}, such that the following equation holds, for all $n,
k_1, \dots, k_n \in \natural$:
\[
                   
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q_n \times Q_{k_1} \times \dots \times Q_{k_n} \times A^{\sum k_i}
		\ar[d]_{1\times 1^n \times G^{\sum k_i}}
		\ar[r]^-{h_{k_1} \times \dots \times h_{k_n}}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\psi_{k_1} \times \dots \times \psi_{k_n}}}}
                                      
	& Q_n \times A^n
		\ar[d]|{1\times G^n}
		\ar[r]^{h_n}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\psi_n}}}
                                 
	& A
		\ar[d]^G
		\\
	Q_n \times Q_{k_1} \times \dots \times Q_{k_n} \times A^{\sum k_i}
		\ar[r]_-{h'_{k_1} \times \dots \times h'_{k_n}}
	& Q_n \times B^n
		\ar[r]_{h'}
	& B \\
}
\hskip 1in
\]
\begin{equation}
\label{weakfunctordef}
\hskip 2in

	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
		\xymatrix{ {} \ar @{}[d]^{=} \\ {} }

                   
\xymatrix{
	Q_n \times Q_{k_1} \times \dots \times Q_{k_n} \times A^{\sum k_i}
		\ar[d]_{1\times 1^n \times G^{\sum k_i}}
		\ar[r]^-{h_{\sum k_i}}
                                        
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1.5,-2.5)\object{\psi_{\sum k_i}}}}
	& A
		\ar[d]^G
		\\
	Q_n \times Q_{k_1} \times \dots \times Q_{k_n} \times B^{\sum k_i}
		\ar[r]_-{h'_{\sum k_i}}
	& B \\
}
\end{equation}
and the diagram
\begin{equation}
\label{weakfunctordef2}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	G a \ar[r]^{\delta'_1} \ar[d]_1
	& h'(1_P, G a) \ar[d]^{\psi_1} \\
	G a \ar[r]_{G \delta_1}
	& G h(1_P, a)
}
\end{equation}
commutes.
The morphism is weak if every $\psi$ is invertible, and
strict if every $\psi$ is an identity.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
This can be established by a straightforward check of the definition.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- defn-65: body_md -->
\label{transfdef}
\index{transformation!between morphisms of algebras for a \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad}
Let $Q, A, B$ etc.\ be as above, and let $(F,\phi), (G,\gamma)$ be lax
morphisms of $Q$-algebras $A \to B$.
A \textbf{$Q$-transformation} $F \to G$ is a natural transformation $\sigma:
F \to G$ such that
\begin{equation}
\xymatrixrowsep{1pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q \circ A \rtwocell^{1\circ F}_{1\circ G}{\sigma} \ar[dd]_\alpha
		\ddrtwocell\omit{\gamma}
	& Q \circ B \ar[dd]^\beta
	& & Q \circ A \ar[r]^{1 \circ F} \ar[dd]_\alpha
		\ddrtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& Q \circ B \ar[dd]^\beta \\
	& & = \\
	A \ar[r]_G
	& B
	& & A \rtwocell^F_G{\sigma}
	& B
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end defn-65 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{inv <=> Q-inv}
A $Q$-transformation $\sigma: (F, \phi) \to (G, \psi)$ is invertible as a
natural transformation if and only if it is invertible as a $Q$-transformation.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
``If'' is obvious: we concentrate on ``only if''. It is enough to show that
$\sigma^{-1}$ is a $Q$-transformation, which is to say that
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
	h(q, Ga_\bullet)
		\ar[r]^\psi
		\ar[d]_{h(q,\sigma^{-1}_{a_\bullet})} &
	Gh(q,a_\bullet)
		\ar[d]^{\sigma^{-1}_{h(q,a_\bullet)}} \\
	h(q, Fa_\bullet)
		\ar[r]^\phi &
	Fh(q,a_\bullet)
}
\end{equation}
commutes for all $(q,a_\bullet) \in Q \circ A$, and this follows
from the fact that ${\sigma_{h(q,a_\bullet)}} \circ \phi = \psi \circ
{h(q,\sigma_{a_\bullet})}$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
There is a chain of monadic adjunctions
\index{adjunctions!for \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads}
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn:cat_adjs}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
  {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-FP-Operad}}}}} \ar@<1.2ex>[d]^{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}_{\Sigma}}}
	 \ar@/r1.7cm/[dd]^{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}_{\rm pl}}}
	 \ar@/r3cm/[ddd]^{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} \\
  \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}} \ar@<1.2ex>[d]^{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}_{\rm pl}}} \ar@<1.2ex>[u]^{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\Sigma}}}_{\dashv}
	 \ar@/r1.7cm/[dd]^{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} \\
  \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}} \ar@<1.2ex>[u]^{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}}_{\dashv} \ar@<1.2ex>[d]^{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}}
	 \ar@/l1.7cm/[uu]^{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}^{\rm pl}}} \\
  \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^\natural \ar@<1.2ex>[u]^{\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}_{\dashv} \ar@/l1.7cm/[uu]^{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} 
  	 \ar@/l3cm/[uuu]^{\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}}
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
This follows from Lemmas \ref{lem:frees_exist} and \ref{lem:monadj}, via an
application of the argument of Theorem \ref{thm:opd monadic over setN}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- defn-66: body_md -->
\index{orthogonal}
Let $e: a \to b$ and $m: c \to d$ be arrows in a category \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}.
We say that $e$ is \textbf{left orthogonal} to $m$, written $e \mathop{\bot} m$, if,
for all arrows $f: a \to c$ and $g: b \to d$ such that $mf = ge$, there exists
a unique map $t: b \to c$ such that the following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrix{
	a \ar[r]^{\forall f} \ar[d]_e
	& c \ar[d]^m \\
	b \ar@{..>}[ur]^{\exists! t} \ar[r]_{\forall g}
	& d
}
\]
<!-- end defn-66 -->
<!-- defn-67: body_md -->
\label{def:FS}
\index{factorization system}
Let \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ be a category.
A \textbf{factorization system} on \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ is a pair $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ of classes of maps
in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item \label{axm:factor} for all maps $f$ in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, there exist $e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ and $m
\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ such that $f = m  e$;
\item \label{axm:iso_closure} \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ contain all identities, and are
closed under composition with isomorphisms on both sides;
\item \label{axm:orthogonal} $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} \mathop{\bot} \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$, i.e. $e \mathop{\bot} m$ for all $e \in
\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ and $m \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-67 -->
<!-- example-15: body_md -->
\label{ex:epi-mono}
\index{factorization system!epi-mono}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} = \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ be the epimorphisms, and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ be the monomorphisms.
Then $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ is a factorization system.
<!-- end example-15 -->
<!-- example-16: body_md -->
More generally, let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ be some variety of algebras,
$\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ be the regular epimorphisms (i.e., the surjections), and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ be the
monomorphisms.
Then $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ is a factorization system.
<!-- end example-16 -->
<!-- example-17: body_md -->
\index{factorization system!bijective on objects/full and faithful!on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Digraph}}}}}
\label{ex:digraphFS}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} = \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Digraph}}}}$, the category of directed graphs and graph morphisms.
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ be the maps bijective on objects, and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ be the full and faithful
maps.
Then $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}},\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ is a factorization system.
<!-- end example-17 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:fact_standard}
Let \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ be a category, and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ be a factorization system on \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} \cap \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is the class of isomorphisms in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}.
\item \label{fact_unique} The factorization in \ref{def:FS} (\ref{axm:factor})
is unique up to unique isomorphism.
\item The factorization in \ref{def:FS} (\ref{axm:factor}) is functorial, in
the following sense: if the square
\[

	\xymatrix{
		A \ar[r]^-{f} \ar[d]_-{g}
		& B \ar[d]^-{h} \\
		C \ar[r]^-{f'}
		& D
	}

\]
commutes, and $f = me, f' = m'e'$, then there is a unique morphism $i$ making
\[
\xymatrix{
	A \ar@{->>}[r]^{e} \ar[d]_g
	& {} \ar@{(>->}[r]^{m} \ar@{..>}[d]_i
	& B \ar[d]^h \\
	C \ar@{->>}[r]^{e'}
	& {} \ar@{(>->}[r]^{m'}
	& D
}
\]
commute.
Thus, given a choice of $e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ and $m \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ for each $f$ in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} (such that
$f = me$), we may construct functors $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}_*, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_* : [\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{2}}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}] \to [\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{2}}}},
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}]$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}_* : f \mapsto e \\
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}_* : (g,h) \mapsto (g,i) \\
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_* : f \mapsto m \\
& \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_* : (g,h) \mapsto (i,h).
\end{eqnarray*}
These functors are determined by \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ uniquely up to unique isomorphism.
\item \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ are closed under composition.
\item $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}^{\bot} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ and ${}^{\bot} \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$, where $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}^{\bot} = \{f
\mbox{ in } \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} : e \mathop{\bot} f \mbox{ for all } e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\}$ and $^{\bot}\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}} = \{f
\mbox{ in } \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} : f \mathop{\bot} m \mbox{ for all } m \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:monad}
Let \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ be a category with a factorization system $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$.
Let $T$ be a monad on \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ and let $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} = \{ f \mathop{\mbox{in}}\ \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} : U f \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\}$
and $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}} = \{f \mathop{\mbox{in}}\ \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} : U f \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\}$, where $U$ is the forgetful functor
$\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
Then $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ is a factorization system on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T$ if $T$ preserves
\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}-arrows.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
This is established in \cite{acc}, Proposition 20.24: however, we shall provide
a proof for the reader's convenience.
We shall establish the axioms listed in Definition \ref{def:FS}.

\ref{axm:factor}.
Take an algebra map
\[

	                                                  
	
	\xymatrix{
		T A \ar[r]^-{T f} \ar[d]_-{a}
		& T B \ar[d]^-{b} \\
		A \ar[r]^-{f}
		& B
	}


\]
Applying axiom \ref{axm:factor} to the factorization system $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$, we
obtain a decomposition $f = m  e$, where $e: A \to I$ and $m: I \to B$.
We wish to lift this to a decomposition of $f$ as an algebra map.
In other words, we need a map $i: TI \to I$ making the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	TA \ar@{->>}[r]^{Te} \ar[d]_a
	& TI \ar[r]^{Tm} \ar@{..>}[d]_i
	& TB \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar@{->>}[r]^e
	& I \ar@{(>->}[r]^m
	& B
}
\]
commute, such that $(I,i)$ is a $T$-algebra.
Since $T$ preserves \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}-arrows, $T e \mathop{\bot} m$, and we may obtain $i$ by
applying this orthogonality to the diagram \[
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	TA \ar[r]^{a} \ar[d]_{T e}
	& A \ar[r]^e
	& I \ar[d]^m \\
	TI \ar[r]_{Tm} \ar@{..>}[urr]^{\exists!i}
	& TB \ar[r]_b
	& B.
}
\]
It remains to show that $(I,i)$ is a $T$-algebra.
For the unit axiom, consider the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	A \ar@{->>}[r]^e \ar[d]^{\eta_A} \ar@/l1cm/[dd]_1
	& I \ar@{(>->}[r]^m \ar[d]^{\eta_I} & B \ar[d]^{\eta_B} \ar@/r1cm/[dd]^1\\
	TA \ar@{->>}[r]^{Te} \ar[d]_a & TI \ar[r]^{Tm} \ar[d]^i & TB \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar@{->>}[r]_e & E \ar@{(>->}[r]_m & B
}
\]
The top squares commute by naturality, and the outside triangles commute since $(A,a)$ and $(B,b)$ are $T$-algebras.
Hence the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	& I \ar@{(>->}[dr]^m \ar@{..>}[dd] \\
	A \ar@{->>}[ur]^e \ar@{->>}[dr]_e & & B \\
	& I \ar@{(>->}[ur]_m
}
\]
commutes if the dotted arrow is either $1_I$ or $i\eta_I$.
By orthogonality, $i\eta_I = 1_I$.

For the multiplication axiom, observe that the diagrams
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	T^2 A \ar@{->>}[r]^{T^2 e} \ar[d]_{\mu_A}
	& T^2 I \ar[r]^{T^2 m} \ar[d]^{\mu_I}
	& T^2 B \ar[d]^{\mu_B} \\
	TA \ar@{->>}[r]^{Te} \ar[d]_a & TI \ar[r]^{Tm} \ar[d]^i & TB \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar@{->>}[r]_e & E \ar@{(>->}[r]_m & B
}
\hskip 1cm
\xymatrix{
	T^2 A \ar@{->>}[r]^{T^2 e} \ar[d]_{T a} \ar@/l1cm/[dd]_{a\mu_A}
	& T^2 I \ar[r]^{T^2 m} \ar[d]^{T i}
	& T^2 B \ar[d]^{T b} \ar@/r1cm/[dd]^{b\mu_B} \\
	TA \ar@{->>}[r]^{Te} \ar[d]_a & TI \ar[r]^{Tm} \ar[d]^i & TB \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar@{->>}[r]_e & E \ar@{(>->}[r]_m & B
}
\]
both commute.
So the diagram
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	T^2 A \ar[r]^{\mu_A} \ar@{->>}[d]_{T^2 e}
		& TA \ar[r]^a & A \ar[r]^e & I \ar@{(>->}[d]^m \\
	T^2 I \ar[r]_{T^2 m} \ar@{..>}[urrr]
		& T^2 B \ar[r]_{\mu_B} & TB \ar[r]_b & B
}
\]
commutes if we take the dotted arrow to be either $i\mu_I$ or $i(Ti)$.
By orthogonality, $i\mu_I = i(Ti)$.

\ref{axm:iso_closure}.  
The image under $U$ of an isomorphism in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T$ is an isomorphism in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}.
The class \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ contains all isomorphisms in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, so $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} = U^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}})$ contains
all isomorphisms in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T$.
By similar reasoning, $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ is closed under composition with isomorphisms,
and $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ also satisfies these conditions.

\ref{axm:orthogonal}.
We wish to show that $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} \mathop{\bot} \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
Take $T$-algebras
\[

	\mbox{$\left(\begin{matrix}
		{T}{A} \cr \phantom{a} \Big\downarrow {a} \cr {A}
	\end{matrix}\right)$}
,

	\mbox{$\left(\begin{matrix}
		{T}{B} \cr \phantom{b} \Big\downarrow {b} \cr {B}
	\end{matrix}\right)$}
,

	\mbox{$\left(\begin{matrix}
		{T}{I} \cr \phantom{i} \Big\downarrow {i} \cr {I}
	\end{matrix}\right)$}
,

	\mbox{$\left(\begin{matrix}
		{T}{J} \cr \phantom{j} \Big\downarrow {j} \cr {J}
	\end{matrix}\right)$}

\]
and algebra maps
\[

	                                                  
	
	\xymatrix{
		T A \ar[r]^-{T e} \ar[d]_-{a}
		& T I \ar[d]^-{i} \\
		A \ar[r]^-{e}
		& I
	}

,

	                                                  
	
	\xymatrix{
		T J \ar[r]^-{T m} \ar[d]_-{j}
		& T B \ar[d]^-{b} \\
		J \ar[r]^-{m}
		& B
	}

,

	                                                  
	
	\xymatrix{
		T A \ar[r]^-{T f} \ar[d]_-{a}
		& T J \ar[d]^-{j} \\
		A \ar[r]^-{f}
		& J
	}

,

	                                                  
	
	\xymatrix{
		T I \ar[r]^-{T g} \ar[d]_-{i}
		& T B \ar[d]^-{b} \\
		I \ar[r]^-{g}
		& B
	}


\]
where the first two maps are in $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ and $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ respectively.
Suppose that $ge = mf$.
Now, $e \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ and $m \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$, so $e \mathop{\bot} m$, and there is a unique map $t$
in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ such that
\[

	\xymatrix{
		A \ar[r]^-{f} \ar[d]_-{e}
		& J \ar[d]^-{m} \\
		I \ar@{..>}[ur]^{\exists! t} \ar[r]^-{g}
		& B
	}

\]
commutes.
We wish to show that $t$ is a map of $T$-algebras.

Consider the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	TA \ar[r]^{Te} \ar[d]_a \ar@/u0.7cm/[rr]^{Tf}
	&TI \ar[r]^{Tt} \ar[d]_i \ar@/u0.7cm/[rr]^{Tg}
	& TJ \ar[r]^{Tm} \ar[d]^j
	& TB \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar[r]^e \ar@/d0.7cm/[rr]_f
	& I \ar[r]^t \ar@/d0.7cm/[rr]_g
	& J \ar[r]^m
	& B
}
\]
We wish to show that the middle square commutes: the assumptions tell us that
all other squares commute.
Recall that $T e \mathop{\bot} m$, and apply orthogonality to the square
\[

	\xymatrix{
		TA \ar[r]^-{j Tf} \ar[d]_-{Te}
		& J \ar[d]^-{m} \\
		TI \ar@{..>}[ur]^{\exists!u} \ar[r]^-{gi}
		& B
	}

\]
Now,
\[
\begin{array}{rcll}
j(Tf)	&= & fa		& \mbox{($f$ is a map of $T$-algebras)} \\
	&= & tea	& \mbox{(Definition of $t$)} \\
	&= & ti(Te)	& \mbox{($e$ is a map of $T$-algebras)} \\
\end{array}
\]
and $mti = gi$ by definition of $t$, so $ti = u$ by uniqueness.
Similarly,
\[
\begin{array}{rcll}
gi	&= & b(Tg)	& \mbox{($g$ is a map of $T$-algebras)} \\
	&= & b(Tm)(Tt)	& \mbox{(Definition of $t$)} \\
	&= & mj(Tt)	& \mbox{($m$ is a map of $T$-algebras)} \\
\end{array}
\]
and $j(Tf) = j(Tt)(Te)$ by definition of $t$, so $j(Tt) = u$ by uniqueness.
Hence $j(Tt) = ti$, and $t$ is a map of $T$-algebras.

By construction, $t$ is unique.
So $e \mathop{\bot} m$ in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T$, so $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}} \mathop{\bot} \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
All the axioms are satisfied, and so $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ is a factorization
system on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^T$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- example-18: body_md -->
\index{factorization system!bijective on objects/full and faithful!on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ be the factorization system on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Digraph}}}}\ described in Example
\ref{ex:digraphFS} above, and let $T$ be the free category monad.
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}\ is monadic over \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Digraph}}}}, and $T$ preserves the property of being
bijective on objects.
Hence, this gives a factorization system $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ on
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}\ where $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ is the collection of bijective-on-objects functors, and
$\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is the collection of full and faithful functors.
<!-- end example-18 -->
<!-- example-19: body_md -->
Similarly, there is a factorization system on $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Digraph}}}}^\natural$, where \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ is
the class of maps that are pointwise bijective on objects, and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ is the
class of maps that are pointwise full and faithful.
This lifts to a factorization system $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ on $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^\natural$, in
which $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ is the class of pointwise bijective-on-objects arrows, and
$\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is the class of pointwise full-and-faithful arrows.
<!-- end example-19 -->
<!-- example-20: body_md -->
\label{ex:catopdFS}
\index{factorization system!bijective on objects/full and faithful!on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}}
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} = \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^\natural$, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ be the pointwise bijective-on-objects maps, and
\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ be those that are pointwise full and faithful.
Since \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}\ is monadic over $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^\natural$ and the monad preserves
bijective-on-objects maps, this gives a factorization system $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$
on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}\ where $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ is the class of levelwise bijective-on-objects
maps, and $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is the class of levelwise full and faithful ones.
Similarly, there is a factorization system $(\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}', \overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}')$ on
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}\, where  $\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}'$ is the class of bijective-on-objects maps, and
$\overline \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}'$ is the class of levelwise full and faithful ones.
<!-- end example-20 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thm:reg epis split in Set^X^T}
If $X$ is a set and $T$ is a monad on \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^X}\ then the regular epis in
\ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^X})^T}\ are the pointwise surjections.
In other words, the forgetful functor $U:\ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^X})^T} \to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^X}$ preserves and
reflects regular epis.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
See again \cite{acc} section 20, in particular Definition 20.21 and Proposition
20.30.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- defn-68: body_md -->
\label{def:weakening}
\index{unbiased!weakening of a plain operad}
\index{weakening!of a plain operad}
The \textbf{unbiased weakening of $P$}, {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}, is the following \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{1-cells:} 1-cells of $D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P$;
\item \emph{2-cells:} if $A, B \in ({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P)_n$, there is a single 2-cell $A
\to B$ if $\epsilon(A) = \epsilon(B)$ (where $\epsilon$ is the counit
of the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}}$), and no 2-cells $A \to B$ otherwise;
\item \emph{Composition of 2-cells:} the composite of two arrows $A \rightarrow
B \rightarrow C$ is the unique arrow $A \rightarrow C$, and in particular, the
arrows $A \rightarrow B$ and $B \rightarrow A$ are inverses;
\item \emph{Operadic composition:} on 1-cells, as in ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P$, and on 2-cells,
determined by the uniqueness property.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end defn-68 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:WkP_characterization}
${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$ is the unique \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$ has the same 1-cells as $D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P$;
\item we may extend the counit $\epsilon_P : {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P \to  P$ to a map of
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}} \to D_* P$, which is full and faithful levelwise.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Immediate.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- defn-69: body_md -->
\label{def:wkpcat}
\index{weak!$P$-category}
A \textbf{weak $P$-category} is an algebra for {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}.
<!-- end defn-69 -->
<!-- defn-70: body_md -->
\index{strict!$P$-category}
A \textbf{strict $P$-category} is an algebra for $D_* P$.
<!-- end defn-70 -->
<!-- defn-71: body_md -->
\index{weak!$P$-functor}
\index{strict!$P$-functor}
Let $(A, h)$ and $(B, h')$ be weak $P$-categories. A \textbf{weak
$P$-functor} from $(A, h)$ to $(B, h')$ is a weak map of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$-algebras.
A \textbf{strict $P$-functor} from $(A, h)$ to $(B, h')$ is a strict map of
${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$-algebras.
<!-- end defn-71 -->
<!-- defn-72: body_md -->
\index{transformation!between $P$-functors}
Let $(F, \phi)$ and $(G, \psi)$ be weak $P$-functors $(A, h) \to (B, h')$. A
\textbf{$P$-transformation} $\sigma: (F, \phi) \to (G, \psi)$ is a
${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$-transformation $(F, \phi) \to (G, \psi)$, in the sense of Definition
\ref{transfdef}.
<!-- end defn-72 -->
<!-- defn-73: body_md -->
A \textbf{$P$-equivalence} is an equivalence in the 2-category \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}.
<!-- end defn-73 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{inv <=> P-inv}
Let $P$ be a plain operad, $(A, h)$ and $(B, h')$ be weak $P$-categories, and
$(F, \phi), (G, \psi) : (A, h) \to (B, h')$ be weak $P$-functors.
A $P$-transformation $\sigma: (F, \phi) \to (G, \psi)$ is invertible as a
$P$-transformation if and only if it is invertible as a natural
transformation.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
This is a straightforward application of Lemma \ref{inv <=> Q-inv}.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- defn-74: body_md -->
\index{trivial monad}
Let \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ be a category, and $(T, \mu, \eta)$ be a monad on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
We say that $(T, \mu, \eta)$ is \textbf{trivial} if $\eta$ is a natural
isomorphism.
<!-- end defn-74 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:triv<=>initial}
The identity monad on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is initial in the category $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Mnd}}}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}})$ of monads on
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, with the unique morphism of monads $(1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, 1, 1) \to (T, \mu, \eta)$ being
$\eta$.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
First we show that $\eta$ is a morphism of monads in the sense of Street 
(Definition \ref{def:monad_morphism}).
One axiom corresponds to the outside of the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
1 \ar[r]^\eta \ar[d]_1 & T \ar[r]^{\eta T} \ar[dr]^1 \ar[d]_1 & T^2 \ar[d]^\mu\\
1 \ar[r]_\eta & T \ar[r]_1 & T
}
\]
commuting; all the inner segments commute (the top right triangle by the unit
axiom for monads), so the outside must commute.
The other axiom corresponds to the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	1 \ar[r]^1 \ar[dr]_\eta & 1 \ar[d]^\eta \\
	& T
}
\]
and this commutes trivially.
Hence, $\eta$ is a morphism of monads $1 \to T$.

Now suppose that $\alpha : 1 \to T$ is a morphism of monads.
From the unit axiom for monad morphisms,  the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
	1 \ar[r]^1 \ar[dr]_\eta & 1 \ar[d]^\alpha \\
	& T
}
\]
must commute, so $\eta = \alpha$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:triv<=>initial}
A monad $(T, \mu, \eta)$ on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is trivial if and only if it is isomorphic to
the identity monad on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
If $T$ is isomorphic to the identity monad, then by Lemma
\ref{lem:triv<=>initial} the isomorphism concerned must be $\eta$, so $\eta$
must be invertible.
It is readily checked that if $\eta$ is invertible, then $\eta^{-1}$ must be a
morphism of monads, so if $T$ is trivial then it is isomorphic to the identity
monad.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- example-21: body_md -->
\emph{The trivial theory:}
\label{ex:trivial_theory}
\index{sets}
Let $0$ be the initial operad, whose algebras are sets.
An unbiased weak $0$-category is a category equipped with a specified trivial
monad, for the following reason.
$0$ has only one operator (call it $I$), of arity one. Hence $({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} 0)_1
\cong \natural$, and all other $({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} 0)_n$'s are empty.
All derived operations in the theory of sets are composites of identities, and
thus equivalent to the identity.
So all objects of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($0$)}}}_1$ are isomorphic.
Hence, $I \cong \mbox{id}$.
All diagrams commute: in particular, those giving the monad and monad morphism
axioms commute, so in any weak $0$-category $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$, the functor
$\hat I$ is a monad, and the isomorphism $\hat I \to 1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is an isomorphism of
monads.
By Corollary \ref{cor:triv<=>initial}, $\hat I$ must be trivial.

Conversely, suppose $T$ is a trivial monad on a category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
We wish to show that $\mu$ is also invertible, and thus that $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is an
unbiased weak $0$-category.
From the monad axioms, we have that
\[
\xymatrix{
	T \ar[r]^{\eta T} \ar[dr]_{\mbox{id}}
	& T^2 \ar[d]^{\mu} \\
	& T
}
\]
commutes.
But $\eta T$ is invertible, so $\mu$ must be its inverse.
So $\mbox{id} \cong T \cong T^2 \cong T^3 \cong \ldots$, and all diagrams
commute.
Hence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is an unbiased weak $0$-category.

If $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, S)$ and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, T)$ are weak $0$-categories, then a weak $0$-functor
$(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, S) \to (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, T)$ is a functor $F: \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ and a natural isomorphism 
$\phi : TF \to FS$, such that the equations 
\[
\xymatrix{
	& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[dl]_S \ar[dd]^S  \ar[rr]^F \ddrrtwocell\omit{^\phi^{-1}}
	& & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} \ar[dd]^T \\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[dr]_S  \\
	& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[rr]_F \uuuppertwocell\omit{<-3>\mu} & & D
}
\xymatrix{{} \\ = \\ {}}
\xymatrix{
	& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[dl]_S \ar[rr]^F \drtwocell\omit{^\phi^{-1}}
	& & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} \ar[dd]^T \ar[dl]_T \\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[dr]_S  \ar[rr]^F 
	& {} \drtwocell\omit{^\phi^{-1}} & D \ar[dr]_T \\
	& \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[rr]_F  & & D \uuuppertwocell\omit{<-3>\mu}
}
\]
and
\[
\xymatrix{
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ddlowertwocell<-10>_{1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}}{^\eta} \ar[dd]^S \ar[rr]^F
		\ddrrtwocell\omit{^\phi^{-1}}
	& & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} \ar[dd]^T \\ \\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[rr]_F & & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}
}
\xymatrix{{} \\ = \\ {}}
\xymatrix{
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}  \ddrrtwocell\omit{^\phi^{-1}} \ar[rr]^F \ar[dd]_{1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}}
	& & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} \dduppertwocell<10>^T{^\eta} \ar[dd]_{1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}} \\ \\
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \ar[rr]_F & & \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}
}
\]
are satisfied.
<!-- end example-21 -->
<!-- example-22: body_md -->
\emph{Pointed sets:}
\label{ex:pointed_sets}
\index{pointed sets}
Let $P$ be the operad with a single element of arity 0 (call it $*$) and a
single element of arity 1 (the identity).
Strict algebras for $P$ in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$ are pointed sets.
The set $({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P)_0$ is countable (it has elements $*, I*, I^2*, I^3*,
\ldots$, and so is $({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P)_1$ (it has elements $\mbox{id}, I, I^2,
\ldots$).
So an unbiased weak $P$-category is a category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ equipped with a
distinguished object $\hat *$ and a trivial monad $\hat I$.

If $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}})$ are unbiased weak $P$-categories,
then a weak $P$-functor $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})) \to (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ is a triple $(F,
\phi, \psi)$, where $F$ and $\phi$ are as in Example \ref{ex:trivial_theory},
$\psi : \bar * \to F \hat *$ is an isomorphism, and there is exactly one
natural isomorphism $\bar I^n \bar * \to F \hat I^m \hat *$ composed from
$\phi$s and $\psi$s for each $m$ and each $n \in \natural$.
<!-- end example-22 -->
<!-- example-23: body_md -->
\emph{Monoids:}
\label{ex:monoids}
\index{monoids}
An unbiased weak $1$-category is precisely an unbiased weak monoidal
category in the sense of Definition \ref{def:umoncat}.
An unbiased weak $1$-functor is an unbiased weak monoidal functor.
For a proof, see \cite{hohc} Theorem 3.2.2.
<!-- end example-23 -->
<!-- example-24: body_md -->
\emph{$M$-sets:}
\label{ex:M-sets}
\index{$M$-sets}
Let $M$ be a monoid, and $N$ be the operad such that
\begin{eqnarray*}
N_1 & = & M \\
N_i & = & \emptyset \mbox{ whenever $i \neq 1$}
\end{eqnarray*}
with composition of arrows of arity 1 given by the multiplication in $M$.
An algebra for $N$ in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}\ is an $M$-set.
An unbiased weak $N$-category is a category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ with a functor $\hat m :
\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ for each $m \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
For every equation $m_1 m_2 \dots m_i = n_1 n_2 \dots n_j$ that is true in $M$,
there is a natural isomorphism $\delta_{m_1 \dots m_i}^{n_1 \dots n_j} : \hat
m_1 \hat m_2 \dots \hat m_i \to \hat n_1 \hat n_2 \dots \hat n_j$.
If $e$ is the identity element in $M$, then $\hat e$ is a trivial monad.
All diagrams involving these natural isomorphisms commute.
Hence, an unbiased weak $N$-category is a category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ together with a weak
monoidal functor $M \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$).
If $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ are unbiased weak $N$-categories, an
unbiased weak $N$-functor is a functor $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ together with natural
transformations $\phi_m : \bar m F \to F \hat m$ for all $m \in M$, such that
if $m_1 m_2 \dots m_i = n_1 n_2 \dots n_j$ in $M$, there is precisely one
natural isomorphism $\bar m_1 \dots \bar m_i F \to F \hat n_1 \dots \hat n_j$
that can be formed by composing $\delta$s and $\phi$s.
<!-- end example-24 -->
<!-- defn-75: body_md -->
\index{weakening!of a symmetric operad}
\label{def:weakening_pres}
Let $\Phi$ be a signature, $P$ be a symmetric operad, and $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}\Phi \to
P$ be a regular epi in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}.
Then the \textbf{weakening} (or \textbf{categorification}) ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$ of
$P$ with respect to $\phi$ is the (unique-up-to-isomorphism) symmetric
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad such that the following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrix{
	D_*{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}\Phi \ar[rr]^{D_* \phi} \ar@{->>}[dr]_b
	&& D_* P \\
	& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}} \ar@{(>->}[ur]_f
}
\]
where $f$ is full and faithful levelwise, $b$ is levelwise bijective on
objects, and $D_*$ is the levelwise discrete category functor $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}} \to
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$.
The existence and uniqueness of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$ follow from Lemma
\ref{lem:fact_standard} applied to the factorization system on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}\
described in \ref{ex:catopdFS} above.
<!-- end defn-75 -->
<!-- defn-76: body_md -->
\label{def:wkPphicat}
\index{weak!$P$-category}
Let $\phi, \Phi$ and $P$ be as above.
A \textbf{$\phi$-weak $P$-category} is an algebra for ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$.
<!-- end defn-76 -->
<!-- defn-77: body_md -->
\index{weak!$P$-functor}
Let $\phi, \Phi$ and $P$ be as above.
A \textbf{$\phi$-weak $P$-functor} is a weak map of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$-algebras.
<!-- end defn-77 -->
<!-- defn-78: body_md -->
\index{weakening!of a symmetric operad}
Let $P$ be a symmetric operad, and $ \xymatrix{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} E \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{e_1} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{e_2} & {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}
\Phi} $ be a presentation for $P$, with $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \to P$ being the
regular epi in Definition \ref{def:opd_presentation}.
The \textbf{weakening of $P$ with respect to $(\Phi, E)$} is the weakening of
$P$ with respect to $\phi$.
<!-- end defn-78 -->
<!-- defn-79: body_md -->
\label{def:wkp}
\index{unbiased!weakening of a symmetric operad}
The \textbf{unbiased} weakening of $P$ is the weakening arising from
the counit $\epsilon: {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \to P$ of the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \dashv
{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}$.
Call this symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}.
<!-- end defn-79 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:explicit_wkp}
Let $\phi, \Phi$ and $P$ be as above.
Then, for every $n \in \natural$, the category ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n$ is the
equivalence relation $\sim$ on the elements of $({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi)_n$, where $t_1 \sim t_2$ if $\phi(t_1) = \phi(t_2)$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Let $n \in \natural$, and $t_1, t_2 \in {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n$.
The objects of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n$ are the elements of $({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi)_n$, by
construction.
Since $\phi_n$ factors through a full functor $\xymatrix{ {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n \ar@{(>->}[r] & (D_*P)_n }$ and $(D_*P)_n$ is the discrete category on
$P_n$, there is an arrow $t_1 \to t_2$ in ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n$ iff $\phi(t_1) =
\phi(t_2)$.
Since this functor is also faithful, such an arrow must be unique.
Hence ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_n$ is a poset; it is readily checked that it is also an
equivalence relation.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- defn-80: body_md -->
\label{def:phi-wkpcat_plain}
Let $P$ be a plain operad, $\Phi$ be a signature, and $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi \to P$ be
a regular epi.
The \textbf{weakening ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$ of $P$ with respect to $\phi$} is the
plain $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$-operad given by the bijective on objects/levelwise full and
faithful factorization
\[
\xymatrix{
	D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi \ar[rr]^{D_* \phi} \ar@{->>}[dr] & & D_* P \\
	& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}} \ar@{(>->}[ur]
}
\]
in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}.
A \textbf{$\phi$-weak $P$-category} is an algebra for ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$.
<!-- end defn-80 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:plain_as_symmetric}
\index{weakening!of a plain operad!considered as a symmetric operad}
Let $P$ be a plain operad, let $\Phi$ be a signature, and let $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi
\to P$ be a regular epi.
Then ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}} \cong {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}})$ in the
category $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
First note that ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}}$ is well-defined: ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}}$ is a
left adjoint, and hence preserves colimits, so ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi$ is a regular epi
in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$.

${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}}$ is defined by its universal property, so it is
enough to show that the \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}})$ also has this
property.
Specifically, it is enough to show that if
\[
\xymatrix{
D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi \ar[rr]^{D_* \phi} \ar@{->>}[dr]_{b} && D_* P \\
& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}} \ar@{(>->}[ur]_f
}
\]
is the bijective-on-objects/full-and-faithful factorization of $\phi$, then in
the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[rr]^{D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi} \ar@{->>}[dr]_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} b}
&& D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P \\
& {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}) \ar@{(>->}[ur]_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} f}
}
\]
the arrow ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} b$ is bijective on objects and the arrow ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} f$ is
levelwise full and faithful (note that $D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} = {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} D_*$).
But this follows straightforwardly from the explicit construction of ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}}$
in Section \ref{sec:explicit_Fs}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a plain operad, $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi \to P$ generate $P$, and $A$ be
a $\phi$-weak $P$-category in the sense of Definition
\ref{def:phi-wkpcat_plain}.
Then $A$ is an ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi$-weak ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$-category in the sense of
Definition \ref{def:wkPphicat}.
Conversely, every ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi$-weak ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$-category is a weak
$P$-category.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
A ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi$-weak ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$-category is a category $A$ and a
morphism ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}} \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(A)$ of symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads.
By Theorem \ref{thm:plain_as_symmetric}, this is equivalent to a morphism
${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}) \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(A)$ in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}$, which is equivalent
by the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}_{\rm pl}}}$ to a morphism of plain
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}} \to {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}_{\rm pl}}} \mathop{\rm{End}}(A)$.
This is exactly a $\phi$-weak $P$-category.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- example-25: body_md -->
\index{monoids}
\index{\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}!as ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} 1$}
Consider the terminal plain operad $1$ whose algebras are monoids.
${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} 1$ is the operad $\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}$ of Example \ref{ex:symmopd}, for which each
$\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}_n$ is the symmetric group $S_n$.
Then the objects of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}$)}}}_n$ are $n$-leafed permuted trees with each node
labelled by a permutation, whereas the 1-cells of $({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($1$)}}})_n$ are
unlabelled permuted trees.
These two sets are not canonically isomorphic.
Hence, there is no canonical isomorphism between ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}$)}}}$ and ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}}
{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($1$)}}}$.
<!-- end example-25 -->
<!-- example-26: body_md -->
\label{ex:trivial_theory_biased}
\index{sets}
Consider the trivial theory (given by the initial operad 0), with the empty
generating set.
A weak algebra for this theory (with respect to this generating set) is simply
a category.
${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}$ is a left adjoint, and hence preserves colimits, so ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}\emptyset$ is
the initial operad, and the coequalizer $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}\emptyset \to 0$ is
therefore the identity.
Hence ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(0)$}}}$ is also the initial operad, and so a $\phi$-weak
0-category is just a category.
A $\phi$-weak $0$-functor is just a functor.
<!-- end example-26 -->
<!-- example-27: body_md -->
\label{ex:ptd_sets}
\index{pointed sets}
Consider the operad $P$ of Example \ref{ex:pointed_sets}, generated by one
nullary operation $*$.
Let $\phi$ be the associated regular epi.
Then ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$ has one nullary object and no objects of any other arity; the only arrow is the identity on the unique nullary object.
In fact, ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}} = D_* P$.
So a weak algebra for this theory and this generating set is a category \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\
with a distinguished object $\hat * \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
A $\phi$-weak $P$-functor from $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ to $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ is a
functor $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ and an isomorphism $\bar * \stackrel{\sim}{\to} \hat *$.
<!-- end example-27 -->
<!-- example-28: body_md -->
\label{ex:ptd_sets_ABCD}
\index{pointed sets}
Consider again the operad $P$ of Example \ref{ex:pointed_sets}, this time
generated by four nullary operations $A,B,C,D$ (which are all set equal to each
other).
Let $\phi$ be the associated regular epi.
Then ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_0$ is the indiscrete category on the four objects $A, B, C,
D$, and ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}_i$ is empty for all other $i \in \natural$.
Hence a $\phi$-weak $P$-category is a category \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\ containing four specified
objects $\hat A, \hat B, \hat C$ and $\hat D$.
These four objects are isomorphic via specified isomorphisms $\delta_{AB},
\delta_{AC}, \delta_{AD}$ etc, and all diagrams involving these isomorphisms
commute:
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{6pc}
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
\hat A \ar[r]^{\delta_{AB}} \ar[dr]_(0.3){\delta_{AD}} \ar[d]_{\delta_{AC}}
& \hat B \ar[d]^{\delta_{BD}} \ar[dl]^(0.3){\delta_{BC}} \\
\hat C \ar[r]_{\delta_{CD}} & \hat D
}
\]
and $\delta_{XY}\delta_{YX} = 1_{\hat X}$ for all $X,Y \in \{A,B,C,D\}$.

Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ be $\phi$-weak $P$-categories.
A $\phi$-weak $P$-functor $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})) \to (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}, (\bar{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ consists of
\begin{itemize}
\item a functor $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$,
\item an isomorphism $\phi_{XY} : \bar X \stackrel{\sim}{\to} F
\hat X$ for all $X \in \{A, B, C, D\}$,
\end{itemize}
such that, for all $X, Y \in \{A, B, C, D\}$, there is precisely one
isomorphism $\bar X \to F \hat Y$ formed by compositions of $\delta$s and
$\phi$s.
<!-- end example-28 -->
<!-- defn-81: body_md -->
\index{symmetric monoidal category}
A \textbf{symmetric monoidal category} is a 7-tuple $\ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)}$, where
\begin{itemize}
\item $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is a category;
\item $\otimes : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \times \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ is a functor;
\item $I$ is an object of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$,
\item $\alpha: A \otimes (B \otimes C) \to (A \otimes B) \otimes C$ is natural
in $A, B, C \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$;
\item $\lambda : I \otimes A \to A$ and $\rho : A \otimes I \to A$ are natural in $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$;
\item $\tau : A \otimes B \to B \otimes A$ is natural in $A, B \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$,
\end{itemize}
$\alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau$ are all invertible, and the following diagrams
commute:
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
& (A \otimes B) \otimes (C \otimes D) \ar[ddr]^\alpha \\
A \otimes (B \otimes (C \otimes D)) \ar[dd]_{1\otimes\alpha} \ar[ur]^\alpha \\
& & ((A \otimes B) \otimes C) \otimes D \\
A \otimes ((B \otimes C) \otimes D) \ar[dr]_\alpha \\
& (A \otimes (B \otimes C) ) \otimes D \ar[uur]_{\alpha \otimes 1}
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
A \otimes (I \otimes C) \ar[rr]^\alpha \ar[ddr]_{1 \otimes \lambda}
& & (A \otimes I) \otimes C \ar[ddl]^{\rho \otimes 1} \\ \\
& A \otimes C
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
A \otimes I \ar[rr]^\tau \ar[ddr]_\rho && I \otimes A\ar[ddl]^\lambda \\ \\
& A
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
(A \otimes B) \otimes C \ar[r]^\tau \ar[d]_{\alpha^{-1}}
& C \otimes (A \otimes B) \ar[d]^\alpha \\
A \otimes (B \otimes C) \ar[d]_{1 \otimes \tau}
& (C \otimes A) \otimes B \ar[d]^{\tau \otimes 1} \\
A \otimes (C \otimes B) \ar[r]^\alpha
& (A \otimes C) \otimes B
}
\hskip 2em
\xymatrix{
A \otimes (B \otimes C) \ar[r]^\tau \ar[d]_\alpha
& (B \otimes C) \otimes A \ar[d]^{\alpha^{-1}} \\
(A \otimes B) \otimes C \ar[d]_{\tau \otimes 1}
& B \otimes (C \otimes A) \ar[d]^{1 \otimes \tau} \\
(B \otimes A) \otimes C \ar[r]^{\alpha^{-1}}
& B \otimes (A \otimes C)
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
A \otimes B \ar[dr]_1 \ar[r]^{\tau_{A,B}} & B \otimes A \ar[d]^{\tau_{B,A}} \\
& A \otimes B.
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end defn-81 -->
<!-- defn-82: body_md -->
Let $M = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)}$ and $N = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', \otimes', I', \alpha', \lambda', \rho',
	\tau')}$ be symmetric monoidal categories.
\index{symmetric monoidal functor}
A \textbf{lax symmetric monoidal functor} $F: M \to N$ consists of
\begin{itemize}
\item a functor $F : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}'$,
\item morphisms $F_2 : (F A) \otimes' (F B) \to F(A \otimes B)$, natural in
$A,B \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$,
\item a morphism $F_0 : I' \to F I$ in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}'$,
\end{itemize}
such that the following diagrams commute:
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn:symm_mon_fctr_assoc}
\xymatrix{
FA \otimes' (FB \otimes' FC) \ar[r]^{\alpha'} \ar[d]_{1 \otimes' F_2}
& (FA \otimes' FB) \otimes' FC \ar[d]^{F_2 \otimes' 1} \\
FA \otimes' (F(B \otimes C)) \ar[d]_{F_2}
& F(A \otimes B) \otimes' FC \ar[d]^{F_2} \\
F(A \otimes (B \otimes C)) \ar[r]^{F\alpha}
& F((A \otimes B) \otimes C)
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn:symm_mon_fctr_unit}
\xymatrix{
(FB) \otimes' I' \ar[r]^{\rho'} \ar[d]_{1 \otimes' F_0}FB
& F B \\
(FB) \otimes' (FI) \ar[r]^{F_2}
& F(B \otimes I) \ar[u]_{F\rho}
}
\hskip 2em
\xymatrix{
I' \otimes' (FB) \ar[r]^{\lambda'}
& FB \\
(FI) \otimes' (FB) \ar[r]^{F_2} \ar[u]^{F_0 \otimes' 1}
& F(I \otimes B) \ar[u]_{F\lambda}
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn:symm_mon_fctr_tau}
\xymatrix{
(FA)\otimes'(FB) \ar[r]^{\tau'} \ar[d]_{F_2}
& (FB) \otimes' (FA) \ar[d]^{F_2} \\
F(A \otimes B) \ar[r]^{F\tau}
& F(B \otimes A).
}
\end{equation}
$F$ is said to be \textbf{weak} when $F_0, F_2$ are isomorphisms, and
\textbf{strict} when $F_0, F_2$ are identities.
\index{lax!symmetric monoidal functor}
\index{weak!symmetric monoidal functor}
\index{strict!symmetric monoidal functor}
<!-- end defn-82 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:smc_coherence}
(Mac Lane) \index{Mac Lane, Saunders}
\index{coherence!for symmetric monoidal categories}
In each weak symmetric monoidal category $M$ there is a function which assigns
to each pair $(\sigma \cdot t_1, \rho \cdot t_2)$ of permuted $\Phi$-trees of
the same arity $n$ a unique natural isomorphism
\[
{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M (\sigma \cdot t_1, \rho \cdot t_2) : (\sigma \cdot t_1)_M
\to (\rho \cdot t_2)_M : M^n \to M
\]
called the \textbf{canonical map} from $\sigma \cdot t_1$ to $\rho \cdot t_2$,
in such a way that the identity of $M$ and all instances of $\alpha, \lambda,
\rho$ and $\tau$ are canonical, and the composite as well as the
$\otimes$-product of two canonical maps is canonical.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
See \cite{catwork} XI.1.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:mon_fctr_coherence}
\index{coherence!for monoidal functors}
Let $M, N$ be monoidal categories, and $F : M \to N$ be a weak monoidal
functor.
For every $n \in \natural$ and every strongly regular $\Phi$-tree $v$ of arity
$n$, there is a unique map $F_v : v_N(F A_1, \dots, F A_n) \to Fv_M(A_1, \dots,
A_n)$ natural in $A_1, \dots, A_n \in M$ and formed by taking composites and
tensors of $F_0$ and $F_2$, such that the diagram
\[

	\xymatrix{
		v_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n) \ar[r]^-{F_{v}} \ar[d]_-{{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_N}
		& Fv_M(A_1, \dots, A_n) \ar[d]^-{F{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M} \\
		w_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n) \ar[r]^-{F_{w}}
		& F(w)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n)
	}

\]
commutes for all $n \in \natural$, all $v, w \in ({\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \Phi)_n$, and all $A_1,
\dots, A_n \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
See \cite{catwork}, p. 257.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm:smcf_coherence}
\index{coherence!for symmetric monoidal functors}
Let $M,N$ be symmetric monoidal categories, and $F:M \to N$ be a weak symmetric monoidal functor.
Let $\sigma\cdot v$ be an $n$-ary\ permuted $\Phi$-tree.
Then there is a unique natural transformation
\[
\xymatrix{
	M^n \ar[r]^{F^n} \ar[d]_{(\sigma\cdot v)_M}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(1,-1)\object{F_{\sigma\cdot v}}}}
	& N^n \ar[d]^{(\sigma\cdot v)_N} \\
	M \ar[r]_F & N
}
\]
formed by composing tensor products of $F_2$ and $F_0$, possibly with their
arguments permuted.
Furthermore, if $\rho\cdot w$ is another permuted $\Phi$-tree, then the diagram
\[

	\xymatrix{
		(\sigma\cdot v)_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n) \ar[r]^-{F_{\sigma\cdot v}} \ar[d]_-{{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_N}
		& F(\sigma \cdot v)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n) \ar[d]^-{F{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M} \\
		(\rho \cdot w)_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n) \ar[r]^-{F_{\rho \cdot w}}
		& F(\rho\cdot w)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n)
	}

\]
commutes.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
\def\mbox{\upshape{perm}}{\mbox{\upshape{perm}}}
Let $F_{\sigma\cdot v}(A_1, \dots, A_n) = F_v(A_{\sigma(1)}, \dots,
A_{\sigma(n)})$, and similarly on morphisms.
Then $F_{\sigma\cdot v}$ has the required type. 
We may decompose ${\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M(\sigma\cdot v, \rho\cdot w)$ as
$\mbox{\upshape{perm}}_M(\sigma,\rho)\ {\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M(v, w)$, where $\mbox{\upshape{perm}}_M(\sigma,\rho) :
F_{\sigma\cdot v} \to F_{\rho\cdot v}$ is a composite of $\tau$s.

Equation \ref{eqn:symm_mon_fctr_tau} and Lemma \ref{lem:mon_fctr_coherence}
together imply that the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
(\sigma\cdot v)_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n)\ar[r]^{F_{\sigma\cdot v}} \ar[d]_{\mbox{\upshape{perm}}_N}
& {F((\sigma \cdot v)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n))} \ar[d]^{F\mbox{\upshape{perm}}_M} \\
(\rho\cdot v)_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n)\ar[r]^{F_{\rho\cdot v}} \ar[d]_{{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_N}
& {F((\rho \cdot v)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n))} \ar[d]^{F{\mbox{\upshape{can}}}_M} \\
{(\rho \cdot w)_N(F A_1, \dots F A_n)} \ar[r]^{F_{\rho \cdot w}}
& {F((\rho\cdot w)_M(A_1, \dots, A_n))}
}
\]
commutes.
It remains to show that $F_{\sigma \cdot v}$ is unique with this property.

Suppose that $F_{\sigma\cdot v}$ is not unique for some $\sigma \cdot v$, and
that there exists some natural transformation $G: (\sigma \cdot v)_N(FA_1,
\dots, FA_n) \to F((\sigma\cdot v)_M (A_1, \dots, A_n))$, composed of tensor
products of components of $F_0$ and $F_2$, such that $G \neq F_{\sigma\cdot
v}$.
Suppose further that $\sigma\cdot v$ and $G$ have been chosen to be a minimal
counterexample, in the sense that of all such counterexamples, $\sigma$ may be
written as a product of the smallest number of transpositions.
If no transpositions are used, then we have a contradiction, because then
$\sigma = 1_n$, and Lemma \ref{lem:mon_fctr_coherence} tells us that $G = F_v$.
But suppose $\sigma = t_1t_2\dots t_m$ where each $t_i$ is a transposition:
then $t_1 \cdot G$ is a natural transformation $(\sigma\cdot v)_N (FA_{t_1
1}, \dots, FA_{t_1 n}) \to F((\sigma\cdot v)_M(A_{t_1 1}, \dots, A_{t_1 n}))$,
and thus a transformation $(t_1\sigma\cdot v)_N (FA_\bullet) \to F((t_1\sigma\cdot v)_M(A_\bullet))$.
But $t_1\sigma = t_2t_3\dots t_m$, and thus (by minimality of $\sigma$), it
must be the case that $t_1 \cdot G = F_{t_1\sigma\cdot v} = t_1\cdot F_{\sigma\cdot
v}$.
Hence $G = F_{\sigma \cdot v}$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
$SM$ is a well-defined ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$-algebra for all $M \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{SMC}}}}$.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The 1-cells of ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$ are the same as those of ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi$; hence, $(\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})$ is
entirely determined on 1-cells by a map of signatures $\Phi \to {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} \mathop{\rm{End}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}})$,
which we have given.
On 2-cells, Theorem \ref{thm:smc_coherence} and the uniqueness property of
2-cells in ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$ tell us that if $\delta_1, \delta_2$ are 2-cells in ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$, then
$\widehat{\delta_1 . \delta_2} = \hat \delta_1 \otimes \hat \delta_2 = \hat
\delta_1 \hat . \hat \delta_2$, and $\widehat{\delta_1 \delta_2} =
\hat{\delta_1} \hat{\delta_2}$ wherever $\delta_1, \delta_2$ are composable.
Hence, $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ is a well-defined ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$-algebra.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
$R(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ is a symmetric monoidal category.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Because there is at most one 2-cell $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ for any pair of 1-cells
$\tau_1, \tau_2$ in ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$, all diagrams involving these commute.
In particular, the axioms for a symmetric monoidal category\ are satisfied.
The 2-cells in $\mathop{\rm{End}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}})$ are natural transformations, so $\alpha, \lambda,
\rho$ and $\tau$ (as images of 2-cells in ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$ under the map $(\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}) : {{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}} \to
\mathop{\rm{End}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}})$) are natural transformations.
All 2-cells in ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$ are invertible, so $\alpha, \lambda, \rho$ and $\tau$ are
all natural isomorphisms.
Hence $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)$ is a symmetric monoidal category.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:RS = 1}
Let \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)}\ be a symmetric monoidal category. Then \[ RS\ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)} = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)}. \]
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Let $RS\ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)} = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes', I', \alpha', \lambda', \rho', \tau')}$.
Their underlying categories are equal, both being $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$.
\[
\begin{array}{rcccl}
\otimes' &= &\hat . &= &\otimes \\
I' &= & \hat e &= & I \\
\alpha' & = &\hat \delta_1 & = & \alpha \mbox{, the unique canonical map of
the correct type}\\
\lambda' & = &\hat \delta_2 & = & \lambda \\
\rho' & = &\hat \delta_3 & = & \rho \\
\tau' & = &\hat \delta_4 & = & \tau \\
\end{array}
\]
<!-- end proof-48 -->
