<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:SR = 1}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ be a ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$-algebra, and let
$(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', (\check{\phantom{\alpha}})) = SR(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$.
Then $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})) = (\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', (\check{\phantom{\alpha}}))$.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Their underlying categories are the same.
As above, $(\check{\phantom{\alpha}})$ is determined on objects by the values it takes on $.$
and $e$: these are $\otimes = \hat .$ and $I = \hat e$ respectively.
So $(\check{\phantom{\alpha}}) = (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})$ on objects.
If $\delta : \tau_1 \to \tau_2$, then $\check \delta$ is the unique canonical
map from $\check \tau_1 \to \check \tau_2$, which, by an easy induction, must be
$\hat \delta$.
So $(\check{\phantom{\alpha}}) = (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})$, and hence $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})) = SR(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:RS = 1 on morphisms}
Let $M = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, \otimes, I, \alpha, \lambda, \rho, \tau)}$ and $N = \ensuremath{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', \otimes', I', \alpha', \lambda', \rho',
	\tau')}$ be symmetric monoidal categories, and let $(F, F_0, F_2)$ be a
weak symmetric monoidal functor $M \to N$.
Then $RS(F, F_0, F_2) = (F, F_0, F_2)$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Let $(G, G_0, G_2) = RS(F, F_0, F_2)$. 
Then $G$ is the underlying functor of $S(F, F_0, F_2)$ which is $F$, and 
$G_0, G_2$ are both the canonical maps with the correct types given by
Theorem \ref{thm:smcf_coherence}: that is to say, they are $F_0$ and $F_2$
respectively.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:SR = 1 on morphisms}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ and $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', (\check{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ be ${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$-algebras, and let $(F,
\phi) : (\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})) \to (\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}', (\check{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ be a weak morphism of
${{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}}$-algebras.
Then $SR(F, \phi) = (F, \phi)$.
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Let  $(G, \gamma) = SR(F, \phi)$.
Then $G$ is the underlying functor of $R(F, \phi)$, which is $F$.
Let $(F, F_0, F_2) = R(F, \phi)$.
Each component of $\gamma$ is then by definition the correct component of the
canonical map arising from $F_0, F_2$ in the process described in Theorem
\ref{thm:smcf_coherence}.
By the ``uniqueness'' part of the Theorem, this must be the corresponding
component of $\phi$.
Hence $\gamma = \phi$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
$S$ and $R$ form an isomorphism of categories $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{SMC}}}} \cong \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Lemmas \ref{lem:RS = 1} and \ref{lem:SR = 1} show that $R$ and $S$ are
bijective on objects; Lemmas \ref{lem:RS = 1 on morphisms} and \ref{lem:SR = 1
on morphisms} show that $R$ and $S$ are locally bijective on morphisms.
Hence, $R$ and $S$ are a pair of mutually inverse isomorphisms of categories.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- defn-83: body_md -->
A (directed) \textbf{multigraph} consists of
\index{multigraph}
\begin{enumerate}
\item a set of \textbf{vertices} $V$,
\item for each $n \in \natural$ and each sequence $v_1, v_2, \dots,
v_n, w$ of vertices, a set $E(v_1, \dots, v_n; w)$ of \textbf{funnels from
$v_1, \dots, v_n$ to $w$}. 
\index{funnel}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-83 -->
<!-- defn-84: body_md -->
Let $M_1 = (V_1, E_1)$ and $M_2 = (V_2, E_2)$ be multigraphs.
\index{morphism!of multigraphs}
A \textbf{morphism of multigraphs} $f: M_1 \to M_2$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item a function $f_V : V_1 \to V_2$,
\item for each finite sequence $v_1, v_2 \dots v_n, w$ of vertices in $M_1$, a
function
\[
f^{v_1,\dots,v_n}_w : E_1(v_1, \dots, v_n; w)
	\to E_2(f_V(v_1), \dots, f_V(v_n); f_V(w)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-84 -->
<!-- defn-85: body_md -->
\index{$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multigraph}}}}_X$}
Let $X$ be a set.
Then $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multigraph}}}}_X$ is the subcategory of $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multigraph}}}}$ whose objects are
multigraphs with vertex set $X$, and whose morphisms are identity-on-vertices
maps of multigraphs.
We define $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X$ and $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Multicat}}}}_X$ similarly.
<!-- end defn-85 -->
<!-- defn-86: body_md -->
\index{multigraph!enriched}
Let \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ be a category.
A \textbf{\ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multigraph} $M = (V,E)$ consists of
\begin{enumerate}
\item a set $V$ of \textbf{vertices},
\item for each $n \in \natural$ and each finite sequence $v_1, v_2 \dots v_n, w$
of vertices, an object of \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}\ called $E(v_1, \dots, v_n; w)$ of
\textbf{funnels from $v_1, \dots, v_n$ to $w$}. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-86 -->
<!-- defn-87: body_md -->
Let $M_1 = (V_1, E_1)$ and $M_2 = (V_2, E_2)$ be \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multigraphs.
A \textbf{morphism of \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}-multigraphs} $f: M_1 \to M_2$ is
\index{morphism!of enriched multigraphs}
\begin{enumerate}
\item a function $f_V : V_1 \to V_2$,
\item for each $n \in \natural$ and each finite sequence $v_1, v_2 \dots v_n,
w$ of vertices in $M_1$, an arrow $E_1(v_1, \dots, v_n; w)
	\to E_2(f_V(v_1), \dots, f_V(v_n); f_V(w))$ in \ensuremath{\mathcal{V}}.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-87 -->
<!-- defn-88: body_md -->
\index{weakening!of a multicategory}
Let $M$ be a plain multicategory with object-set $X$, and let $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}\Phi
\to M$ be a regular epi in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X$.
Then the \textbf{weakening of $M$ with respect to $\phi$} is the
unique-up-to-isomorphism \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-multicategory ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(M)$}}}$ such that the
following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrix{
	D_* F\Phi \ar[rr]^{D_*\phi} \ar@{->>}[dr]_b
	&& D_* M \\
	& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(M)$}}} \ar@{(>->}[ur]_f
}
\]
where $f$ is locally full and faithful, and $b$ is locally bijective on objects
(i.e., each map of sets of funnels in $b$ is a bijection).
The uniqueness of ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(M)$}}}$ follows from properties of the factorization
system on $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Multicat}}}}_X$\ given above.
<!-- end defn-88 -->
<!-- defn-89: body_md -->
\index{unbiased!weakening of a multicategory}
Let $M$ be a (symmetric) multicategory.
The \textbf{unbiased weakening} of $M$ is the weakening of $M$ with respect to
the counit $\epsilon$ of the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}}$ (respectively, the
adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}}$).
<!-- end defn-89 -->
<!-- defn-90: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a multicategory, and let $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}\Phi \to M$ be a regular epi in
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X$.
A \textbf{$\phi$-weak $M$-algebra} is an algebra for ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(M)$}}}$.
An \textbf{unbiased weak $M$-algebra} is an algebra for ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($M$)}}}$.
<!-- end defn-90 -->
<!-- example-29: body_md -->
Let $M$ be the multicategory generated by
\[
\xymatrix{0 \ar[r]^f & 1 \ar[r]^g & 2}
\]
Then a weak algebra for $M$ in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}\ with respect to this generating set
consists of a diagram
\[
\xymatrix{\hat 0 \ar[r]^{\hat f} & \hat 1 \ar[r]^{\hat g} & \hat 2}
\]
in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}, whereas an unbiased weak $M$-algebra is a diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
\hat 0 \ar[dr]_{\hat f} \ar[rr]^{\widehat{gf}} \rrlowertwocell\omit{<3>\sim}
\ar@(ul,dl)[]_{\widehat{I_0}}
& & \hat 2 \ar@(ur,dr)[]^{\widehat{I_2}} \\
& \hat 1 \ar[ur]_{\hat g} \ar@(dl,dr)[]_{\widehat{I_1}}
}
\]
where $\widehat{I_0}, \widehat{I_1}$ and $\widehat{I_2}$ are trivial monads.
<!-- end example-29 -->
<!-- example-30: body_md -->
\index{$M$-sets}
Consider the theory $T$ whose algebras are a monoid $M$ together with an
$M$-set $A$.
Then a weak $T$-algebra with respect to the standard presentation (a binary and
nullary operation on $M$, and an operation $M \times A \to A$) is a classical
monoidal category $\hat M$, a category $\hat A$, and a weak monoidal
functor $\hat M \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(\hat A)$.
An unbiased weak $T$-algebra is an unbiased monoidal category $\hat M$, a
category $\hat A$ equipped with a trivial monad $\hat I_A$, and an unbiased
monoidal functor $\hat M \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(\hat A)$ which commutes up to coherent
isomorphism with $\hat I_A$.
<!-- end example-30 -->
<!-- example-31: body_md -->
\index{weak!$P$-functor}
Let $P$ be an operad, and let $\bar P$ be the multicategory from Section
\ref{sec:Pbar} whose algebras are pairs of $P$-algebras with a morphism between
them.
It seems clear that an unbiased weak $\bar P$-category is a pair of unbiased
weak $P$-categories and an unbiased weak $P$-functor between them; a rigorous
proof would first require a coherence theorem to be proven for weak maps of
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$-operad algebras, and currently no such theorem is known.
<!-- end example-31 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
There is a factorization system $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ on {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-FP-Operad}}}}}\, where \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}\ is the
collection of maps which are bijective on objects, and \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}\ is the collection of
maps which are levelwise full and faithful.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
The proof is exactly as for the proof of existence of the factorization systems
on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}\ and \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}\ given in Example \ref{ex:catopdFS}.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
Let $P$ be the finite product operad\ whose algebras are commutative monoids, and $D_* : {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{FP-Operad}}}}}
\to {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-FP-Operad}}}}}$ be the levelwise ``discrete category'' functor.
Let $Q$ be the finite product \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad\ given by the factorization
\[
\xymatrix{
D_* {\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} P \ar[rr]^{D_* \epsilon_P} \ar@{->>}[dr] & & D_* P \\
& Q \ar@{(>->}[ur]
}
\]
Then an algebra for $Q$ is an unbiased symmetric monoidal category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ such
that, for all $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, the component $\tau_{AA}$ of the symmetry map $\tau$
is the identity on $A \otimes A$.
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
\def\left[1 \atop 1\right]{\left[1 \atop 1\right]}
We adopt the notation for elements of $P$ introduced in Example
\ref{ex:comm_monoid_fp}.
Let $f$ be the unique function ${\underline{2}} \to {\underline{1}}$, and let $t : {\underline{2}} \to {\underline{2}}$
be the permutation transposing 1 and 2.
Then $\epsilon(f \cdot \left[1 \atop 1\right]) = [2] \in P_1$.
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, (\hat{\phantom{\alpha}}))$ be a $Q$-algebra.
We shall write $\hat \left[1 \atop 1\right](A, B)$ as $A \otimes B$.
We may impose a symmetric monoidal category structure on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, where the
symmetry map is the image under $(\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})$ of the unique map $\delta : \left[1 \atop 1\right]
\to t \cdot \left[1 \atop 1\right]$ in $Q_1$.
All diagrams in $Q_1$ commute, so in particular, the following diagram
commutes:
\[
\xymatrix{
	[2] \ar[r] & f\cdot\left[1 \atop 1\right] \\
	f\cdot\left[1 \atop 1\right] \ar[ur]_{f\cdot\delta} \ar[u]
}
\]
The two unlabelled arrows are mutually inverse.
Applying $(\hat{\phantom{\alpha}})$ to the entire diagram, and evaluating the resulting
functors at $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, we see that the following diagram commutes:
\[
\xymatrix{
	\hat{[2]}(A) \ar[r] & A \otimes A \\
	A \otimes A \ar[ur]_{\tau_{A A}} \ar[u]
}
\]
and hence $\tau_{A A} = 1_{A \otimes A}$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- defn-91: body_md -->
\index{strictification}
Let $P$, $Q$, $h$, $A$, $\iota$ be as above. The \textbf{strictification of
$A$}, written \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}), is given by the bijective-on-objects/full and
faithful factorization of $h(\iota \circ 1)$ in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$:
\[
\xymatrix{
	P\circ A \ar[r]^{\iota \circ 1} \ar@{->>}[dr] & Q \circ A \ar[r]^h & A. \\
	& \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) \ar@{(>->}[ur]
}
\]
<!-- end defn-91 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) is a strict $P$-category.
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
It is clear that the action we have defined is strict and associative on
objects and that $1_P$ acts as a unit: we must show that the action on arrows
is associative.
Let $f_i^j:(p_i^j, a_{i\bullet}^j) \to (q_i^j, b_{i\bullet}^j)$, $\sigma \in Q_n$, and
$\tau_i \in Q_{k_i}$ for $j = 1, \dots, k_i$ and $i = 1,\dots,n$.
We wish to show that $h'(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), f_\bullet^\bullet) = h'(\sigma,
h'(\tau_1, f_1^\bullet), \dots, h'(\tau_n, f_n^\bullet))$.

The LHS is
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet), a_\bullet^\bullet)&
	
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_i)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet)}^{-1}}}{\longrightarrow}}
&
h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), h(p_1^1, a_{1\bullet}^1), \dots, h(p_n^{k_n},
a_{n\bullet}^{k_n}))\\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), f_\bullet^\bullet)}}{\longrightarrow}}

&h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), h(q_1^1, b_{1\bullet}^1), \dots, h(q_n^{k'_n},
b_{n\bullet}^{k'_n}))\\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet)}}}{\longrightarrow}}

&h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet), b_\bullet^\bullet).
\end{array}
\]

The RHS is 
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet), a_\bullet^\bullet)&
	
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_i\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet))}^{-1}}}{\longrightarrow}}
&
h(\sigma, h(\tau_1\circ(p_1^\bullet), a_{1\bullet}^\bullet), \dots,
		h(\tau_n\circ(p_n^\bullet), a_{n\bullet}^\bullet)) \\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h(\sigma, h'(\tau_\bullet, f_\bullet^\bullet))}}{\longrightarrow}}

&h(\sigma, h(\tau_1\circ(q_1^\bullet), b_{1\bullet}^\bullet), \dots,
		h(\tau_n\circ(q_n^\bullet), b_{n\bullet}^\bullet))\\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_i\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet))}}}{\longrightarrow}}

&h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet), b_\bullet^\bullet),
\end{array}
\]
where each $h'(\tau_i, f_i^\bullet)$ is
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
h(\tau_i\circ(p_i^\bullet),a_i^\bullet))
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\tau_i\circ(p_i^\bullet)}^{-1}}}{\longrightarrow}}

& h(\tau_i, h(p_i^1, a_{i\bullet}^1), \dots, h(p_i^{k_i}, a_{i\bullet}^{k_i}))\\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h(\tau_i, f_i^\bullet)}}{\longrightarrow}}

& h(\tau_i, h(q_i^1, b_{i\bullet}^1), \dots, h(q_i^{k_i}, b_{i\bullet}^{k_i}))\\
	&
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{\delta_{\tau_i\circ(p_i^\bullet)}}}{\longrightarrow}}

&h(\tau_i\circ(q_i^\bullet),b_i^\bullet).
\end{array}
\]

So the equation holds if the following diagram commutes:

\[
\xymatrix @+10pt {
        
& h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet), a_\bullet^\bullet)
	\ar[dl]_{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_i)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet)}^{-1}}
	\ar[dr]^{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_i\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet))}^{-1}}
	\ar[d]|{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet)}^{-1}} \\
        
h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), h(p_\bullet^\bullet, a_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[d]|{h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), f_\bullet^\bullet)}
& h(\sigma, h(\tau_\bullet\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet),a_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[l]^{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)}}
	\ar[d]|{h(\sigma, h(\tau_i, f_i^\bullet))}
	        
	\ar @{} [dl]|*+[o][F-]{1}
	\ar @{} [dr]|*+[o][F-]{2}
& h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), h(p_\bullet^\bullet, a_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[l]^{h(\sigma, \delta_{\tau_\bullet\circ(p_\bullet^\bullet)}^{-1})}
	\ar[d]|{h(\sigma, h'(\tau_\bullet, f_\bullet^\bullet))}\\
        
h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet), h(q_\bullet^\bullet, b_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[dr]_{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet)}}
& h(\sigma, h(\tau_\bullet\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet), b_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[d]|{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet))}}
	\ar[l]^{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)}}
	\ar[r]_{h(\sigma, \delta_{\tau_i\circ(p_i^\bullet)})}
& h(\sigma, h(\tau_\bullet\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet), b_\bullet^\bullet))
	\ar[dl]^{\delta_{\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet))}}\\
        
&h(\sigma\circ(\tau_\bullet)\circ(q_\bullet^\bullet), b_\bullet^\bullet)\\
}
\]
The triangles all commute because all $\delta$s are images of arrows in $Q$,
and there is at most one 2-cell between any two 1-cells in $Q$. \ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{2}}}
commutes by the definition of $h'(\tau_i, f_i^\bullet)$, and \ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{1}}}
commutes by naturality of $\delta$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:equiv<=>Q-equiv}
Let $Q\circ A 
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h}}{\longrightarrow}}
 A$ and $Q \circ B 
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h'}}{\longrightarrow}}
 B$
be weak $P$-categories, $(F, \pi):A \to B$ be a weak $P$-functor, and $(F, G,
\eta, \epsilon)$ be an adjoint equivalence in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}.
Then $G$ naturally carries the structure of a weak $P$-functor, and $(F, G,
\eta, \epsilon)$ is an adjoint equivalence in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
We want a sequence $(\psi_\bullet)$ of natural transformations:
\[
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q_i\times B^i
		\ar[d]_{1\times G^i}
		\ar[r]^{h'_i}

		& B \ar[d]^G \\
	Q_i\times A^i \ar[r]_{h_i}

}

Let $\psi_i$ be given by
\def

1{

\[
\xymatrixrowsep{3.5pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q_i \times B^i
		\ar[d]_{1\times G^i}
		\ar[r]^{h'_i}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\psi_i}}}
                           
	& B
		\ar[d]^G \\
	Q_i \times A^i
		\ar[r]_{h_i}
	& A \\
}

	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}

\xymatrixrowsep{1.5pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{1.2pc}
\xymatrix{
	Q_i \times B^i

	&& B

		\\

	\ultwocell\omit{<-0.7>*{!(-2,-1.8){1\times \epsilon^{i}}}}

	&& A

\]
We must check that $\psi$ satisfies (\ref{weakfunctordef}) and
(\ref{weakfunctordef2}) from Lemma \ref{lem:wkfunc_explicit}.
For (\ref{weakfunctordef}):
\begin{eqnarray*}
                   

	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}

 &

		\xymatrix{ {} \ar @{}[d]^{=} \\ {} }

& \xymatrixrowsep{5pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{5pc}
\xymatrix{
	{}
		\ar[d]_{1\times G^{\sum k_i}}
		\ar[r]^{h'_{k_1} \times \dots \times h'_{k_n}}

		\ar[r]_h

&

& \xymatrixrowsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrix{

		\ar[rr]^1

	&& {}
		\ar[urur]|{1 \times F^n}
		\ar[rr]_1
	&& {}
		\ar[urur]|{1 \times F^n}

& \xymatrixrowsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrix{
	{}
		\ar[rr]^1

&

& \xymatrixrowsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{2.3pc}
\xymatrix{
	{}
		\ar[rr]^1
		\ar[dd]_{1\times G^{\sum k_i}}
	&& {}
		\ar[rr]^{h'_{\sum k_i}}
                                                         
	& {}
	& {}
		\ar[dd]^G
                                   
		\\

	\ultwocell\omit{<-0.7>*{!(-2,-1.2){1\times \epsilon^{\sum k_i}}}}

For (\ref{weakfunctordef2}), consider the following diagram:
\[
\xymatrix{
	                                          
	&&G b \ar[r]^{\delta_{1_Q}} \ar@/l3cm/[ddd]_{1} \ar[d]_{\eta G}
	  \ar @{} [dr]|*+[o][F-]{2}        
	  & h(1_P, G b) \ar@/r3cm/[ddd]^{\psi_1} \ar[d]^{\eta} \\
	\ar @{} [drr]|*+[o][F-]{1}        
	&&GFG b \ar[r]^{GF\delta_{1_Q}} \ar[d]_{1}
	  \ar @{} [dr]|*+[o][F-]{3}        
	  & GFh(1_P, Gb) \ar[d]^{\pi^{-1}_1}
	  \ar @{} [drr]|*+[o][F-]{5}        
	  \\
	&&GFG b \ar[r]_{G\delta'_{1_Q}} \ar[d]_{G\epsilon}
	  \ar @{} [dr]|*+[o][F-]{4}        
	  & G h'(1_P, FGb) \ar[d]^{Gh'(1_P, \epsilon)} &&\\
	&&Gb \ar[r]_{G\delta'_{1_Q}}
	  & Gh'(1_P, b)
}
\]
(\ref{weakfunctordef2}) is the outside of the diagram.
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{1}}} commutes by the triangle identities.
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{2}}} commutes by naturality of $\eta$.
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{3}}} commutes since $(F, \pi)$ is a $P$-functor.
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{4}}} commutes by naturality of $\delta$.
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{5}}} is the definition of $\psi$.
Hence the whole diagram commutes, and $(G, \psi)$ is a $P$-functor.

To see that $(F, G, \eta, \epsilon)$ is a $P$-equivalence, it is now enough to
show that $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ are $P$-transformations, since they satisfy the
triangle identities by hypothesis.

Write $(GF, \chi) = (G, \psi) \circ (F, \pi)$.
We wish to show that $\eta$ is a $P$-transformation $(1,1) \to (GF, \chi)$.
Each $\chi_{q, a_\bullet}$ is the composite
\[
\xymatrix{
	h(q, GFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{\psi_{q, Fa_\bullet}}
	& G h(q, Fa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{G\pi_{q,a_\bullet}}
	& GFh(q, a_\bullet)
}
\]
Applying the definition of $\psi$, this is
\[
\centerline{
\xymatrix{
	h(q, GFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^\eta
	& GF h(q, GFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{G\pi^{-1}}
	& G h(q, FGFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{Gh_q \epsilon F}
	& Gh(q, F a_\bullet)   \ar[r]^{G\pi}
	& GFh(q, a_\bullet)
}
}
\]

The axiom on $\eta$ is the outside of the diagram
\[
\centerline{
\xymatrix{
	        
	h(q, a_\bullet) \ar[rrrr]^1 \ar[dd]_{h(q, \eta)} \ar[dr]^\eta
	&&&& h(q, a_\bullet) \ar[dd]^\eta \\
	        
	& GFh(q, a_\bullet) \ar[r]^{G\pi^{-1}} \ar[d]|{GFh(q, \eta)}
	\ar @{} [l]|*+[o][F-]{1}        
	\ar @{} [dr]|*+[o][F-]{2}        
	& Gh(q, Fa_\bullet) \ar[d]|{Gh(q, F\eta)} \ar[dr]^1
	        
	\ar @{} [rr]|*+[o][F-]{3} & & \\        
	h(q, GFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^\eta
	& GFh(q, GFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{G\pi^{-1}}
	& Gh(q, FGFa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{Gh(q, \epsilon F)}
	& Gh(q, Fa_\bullet) \ar[r]^{G\pi}
	& GFh(q, a_\bullet)
}
}
\]
\ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{1}}} commutes by naturality of $\eta$, \ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{2}}} commutes by
naturality of $\pi^{-1}$, and \ensuremath{\xymatrix{*+[o][F-]{3}}} commutes since $G\pi \circ G\pi^{-1}
= G(\pi \circ \pi^{-1}) = G1 = 1G$. The triangle commutes by the triangle
identities. So the whole diagram commutes, and $\eta$ is a $P$-transformation.
By Lemma \ref{inv <=> P-inv}, $\eta^{-1}$ is also a $P$-transformation.
Similarly, $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon^{-1}$ are $P$-transformations.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{mainthm}
\index{coherence!for weak $P$-categories}
Let $Q\circ A 
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{h}}{\longrightarrow}}
 A$ be a weak $P$-category. Then $A$
is equivalent to $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A})$ in the 2-category \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}.
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Let $F: \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) \to A$ be given by $F(p, a_\bullet) = h(p, a_\bullet)$ and
identification of maps. This is certainly full and faithful, and it is
essentially surjective on objects because $\delta^{-1}_{1_Q}: h(1_P, a)
\to a$ is an isomorphism. By Lemma \ref{lem:equiv<=>Q-equiv}, it remains only
to show that $F$ is a weak $P$-functor.

We must find a sequence $(\phi_i : h_i (1 \times F^i) \to Fh')$ of natural
transformations satisfying equations (\ref{weakfunctordef}) and
(\ref{weakfunctordef2}) from Lemma \ref{lem:wkfunc_explicit}.
We can take $(\phi_i)_{q, (p_\bullet, a_\bullet^\bullet)} = (\delta_{q \circ(p_\bullet)})_{a_\bullet^\bullet}$
for $q \in Q_n$ and $(p_1, a^1_\bullet), \dots, (p_n, a^n_\bullet) \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A})$.
For (\ref{weakfunctordef}), we must show that

\[
                   
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	{}
		\ar[d]_{1\times F^{\sum k_i}}
		\ar[r]^{h'_{k_1} \times \dots \times h'_{k_n}}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\phi_{k_1} \times \dots \times \phi_{k_n}}}}
                                  
	& {}
		\ar[d]|{1\times F^n}
		\ar[r]^{h'_n}
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\phi_n}}}
                           
	& {}
		\ar[d]^F
		\\
	{}
		\ar[r]_{h_{k_1} \times \dots \times h_{k_n}}
	& {}
		\ar[r]_h
	& {} \\
}

	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
		\xymatrix{ {} \ar @{}[d]^{=} \\ {} }

                   
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	{}
		\ar[d]_{1\times F^{\sum k_i}}
		\ar[r]^{h'_{\sum k_i}}
                                    
		\drtwocell\omit{^*{!(-1,-1.5)\object{\phi_{\sum k_i}}}}
	& {}
		\ar[d]^F
		\\
	{}
		\ar[r]_{h_{\sum k_i}}
	& {} \\
}
\]

All 2-cells in this equation are instances of $\delta$. Since there is at most
one 2-cell between two 1-cells in $Q$, the equation holds.

For (\ref{weakfunctordef2}) to hold, we must have 
\begin{equation}
\label{Fwkfctr}
\xymatrix{
	F(p,a_\bullet) \ar[d]_1 \ar[r]^{\delta_{1_Q}}
	  & h(1_P, F(p,a_\bullet)) \ar[d]^{\phi_{1_P}} \\
	F(p,a_\bullet) \ar[r]_{F\delta'_{1_Q}}
	  & Fh'(1_P,(p, a_\bullet))
}
\end{equation}
Since \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) is a strict monoidal category, $\delta' = 1$.
Apply this observation, and the definitions of $F$, $\phi$ and $h'$; then
(\ref{Fwkfctr}) becomes
\[
\xymatrix{
	h(p,a_\bullet) \ar[d]_1 \ar[r]^{\delta_{1_Q}}
	  & h(1_P, h(p,a_\bullet)) \ar[d]^{\delta_{1_P\circ(p)}} \\
	h(p,a_\bullet) \ar[r]_1
	  & h(p,a_\bullet)
}
\]
Since there is at most one arrow between two 1-cells in $Q$, this diagram
commutes.
So $(F,\phi)$ is a weak $P$-functor, and hence (by Lemma
\ref{lem:equiv<=>Q-equiv}) an equivalence in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- example-32: body_md -->
\index{sets}
Consider the initial operad $0$, whose algebras are sets.
We saw in Example \ref{ex:trivial_theory} that unbiased weak $0$-categories
are categories equipped with a trivial monad.
By Theorem \ref{mainthm}, every unbiased weak $0$-category is equivalent via
weak $0$-functors to a category equipped with a monad which \emph{is} the
identity: in other words, a category.
<!-- end example-32 -->
<!-- example-33: body_md -->
\index{monoids}
Consider the terminal operad $1$, whose algebras are monoids.
Theorem \ref{mainthm} tells us that every unbiased weak monoidal category is
monoidally equivalent to a strict monoidal category.
<!-- end example-33 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
Let $U'$ be the forgetful functor $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Str-$P$-Cat}}}} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}$ (considering both of
these as 1-categories). Then {\rm\textbf{st} } is left adjoint to $U'$.
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
For each $(A,h) \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}$, we construct an
initial object $A 
  \mathop{\stackrel{\scriptstyle{(F', \psi)}}{\longrightarrow}}
 \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A})$ of the comma category
$(A\downarrow U')$, thus showing that {\rm\textbf{st} } is functorial and that ${\rm\textbf{st} }
\dashv U'$ (and that $(F', \psi)$ is the component of the unit at $A$).  Let
$(B, h'')$ be a strict $P$-category, and
$(G, \gamma): A \to U'B$ be a weak $P$-functor. We must show that there is a
unique strict $P$-functor $H$ making the following diagram commute:
\begin{equation}
\label{A->U}
\xymatrix{
	& A \ar[ddl]_{(F', \psi)} \ar[ddr]^{(G, \gamma)} \\ \\
	U'\,\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) \ar@{-->}[rr]^{(H, {\rm id})} & & U'B
}
\end{equation}
$(F', \psi)$ is given as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item If $a \in A$, then ${F'}(a) = (1, a)$.
\item If $f: a \to a'$ in $A$ then ${F'}f$ is the lifting of $h(1,f)$ with
source $(1, a)$ and target $(1, a')$.
\item Each $\psi_{(p, a_\bullet)}$ is the lifting of $(\delta_{1_Q})_{h(p, a_\bullet)}:
h(p, a_\bullet) \to h(1, h(p, a_\bullet))$ to a morphism
$h'(p, F'(a)_\bullet) = (p, a_\bullet) \to (1, h(p, a_\bullet)) = F'(h(p, a_\bullet))$.
\end{itemize}
For commutativity of (\ref{A->U}), we must have $H(1, a) = G(a)$, and
for strictness of $H$, we must have $H(p, a_\bullet) = h''(p, H(1, a)_\bullet)$. These
two conditions completely determine $H$ on objects.

Now, take a morphism $f:(p, a_\bullet) \to (p', a_\bullet')$, which is a lifting of a
morphism $g: h(p,a_\bullet) \to h(p',a_\bullet')$ in $A$.
Then $Hf$ is a morphism $h''(p, Ga_\bullet) \to h''(p', Ga_\bullet')$: the obvious
thing for it to be is the composite
\[
\xymatrix{
	h''(p, Ga_\bullet) \ar[r]^\gamma 
	& G h''(p, a_\bullet) \ar[r]^{Gg}
	& G h''(p', a_\bullet') \ar[r]^{\gamma^{-1}}
	& h''(p', Ga_\bullet')
}
\]
and we shall show that this is in fact the only possibility.
Consider the composite
\[
\xymatrix{
	(1, h(p, a_\bullet)) \ar[r]^-{\psi^{-1}}
	&(p, a_\bullet) \ar[r]^{f}
	& (p', a_\bullet) \ar[r]^-{\psi}
	& (1, h(p', a_\bullet'))
}
\]
in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}). Composition in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A}) is given by composition in $A$, so this is
equal to the lifting of $\delta_{1_Q} \circ g \circ \delta_{1_Q}^{-1} = h(1,
g)$ to a morphism $(1, h(p, a_\bullet)) \to (1, h(p',
a_\bullet'))$, namely $F'g$. So $f = \psi^{-1} \circ F'g \circ \psi$, and
$Hf = H\psi^{-1} \circ HF'g \circ H\psi$. By commutativity of
(\ref{A->U}), $HF' = G$ and $H\psi = \gamma$, so $Hf = \gamma^{-1} \circ
Gg \circ \gamma$ as required.

This completely defines $H$. So we have constructed a unique
$H$ which makes (\ref{A->U}) commute and which is strict. Hence $(F',
\psi): A \to U'\,\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{st}}}}(\ensuremath{A})$ is initial in $(A\downarrow U')$, and so ${\rm\textbf{st} }
\dashv U'$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- example-34: body_md -->
\index{sets}
Consider again the initial operad $0$, whose algebras are sets.
We saw in Example \ref{ex:trivial_theory} that unbiased weak $0$-categories
are categories equipped with a specified trivial monad.
Let $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Triv}}}}$ denote the category of such categories, with morphisms being
functors that preserve the trivial monad up to coherent isomorphism.
A strict unbiased $0$-category is a category equipped with a monad equal to
the identity monad, which is simply a category.
So $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$ is a weakly coreflective sub-2-category of $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Triv}}}}$.
<!-- end example-34 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:fork}
In \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}, if $
	\xymatrix{P \ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{\alpha} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{\beta} & Q \ar[r]^-{\gamma} & R }
$ is a fork, and $\gamma$
is levelwise full and faithful, then $\alpha \cong \beta$.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
We shall construct an invertible \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-$\Sigma$-operad transformation $\eta:\alpha \to
\beta$.
We form the $\eta_n$s as follows: for all $p \in P_n$, let $\gamma\alpha(p) =
\gamma\beta(p)$.
Since $\gamma$ is levelwise full, there exists an arrow $(\eta_n)_p: \alpha(p)
\to \beta(p)$ such that $\gamma_n((\eta_n)_p) = 1_{\gamma\alpha(p)}$.
Since $\gamma$ is levelwise full and faithful, this arrow is an isomorphism.
Each $\eta_n$ is natural because, for all $n \in \natural$ and $f: p \to q$ in
$P_n$,  the image under $\gamma$ of the naturality square
\[
\xymatrix{
	\alpha(p) \ar[r]^{(\eta_n)_p} \ar[d]_{\alpha(f)}
	& \beta(p) \ar[d]^{\beta(f)} \\
	\alpha(q) \ar[r]^{(\eta_n)_q}
	& \beta(q)
}
\]
is
\[
\xymatrix{
	\gamma\alpha(p) \ar[r]^1 \ar[d]_{\gamma\alpha(f)}
	& \gamma\beta(p) \ar[d]^{\gamma\beta(f)} \\
	\gamma\alpha(q) \ar[r]^1
	& \gamma\beta(q)
}
\]
which commutes since $\gamma\alpha = \gamma\beta$.
Since $\gamma$ is faithful, the naturality square commutes, and $\eta_n$ is
natural.
It remains to show that the collection $(\eta_n)_{n \in \natural}$ forms a
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-$\Sigma$-operad transformation, in other words that the equations
{\def{#}_n \times {#}_\bullet1{{#1}_n \times {#1}_\bullet}
\def_{\sum{k_i}}{_{\sum{k_i}}}
\begin{eqnarray}
\xymatrixrowsep{5pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{5pc}
\xymatrix{
	{P}_n \times {P}_\bullet \rtwocell^{{\alpha}_n \times {\alpha}_\bullet}_{{\beta}_n \times {\beta}_\bullet}
		{*{!(-3.5,0)\object{{\eta}_n \times {\eta}_\bullet}}}
		\ar[d]_\circ
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& {Q}_n \times {Q}_\bullet \ar[d]^\circ \\
	P_{\sum{k_i}} \ar[r]_{\beta_{\sum{k_i}}} & Q_{\sum{k_i}}
}
&
	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
		\xymatrix{ {} \ar @{}[d]^{=} \\ {} }

&\xymatrixrowsep{5pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{5pc}
\xymatrix{
	{P}_n \times {P}_\bullet \ar[r]^{{\alpha}_n \times {\alpha}_\bullet}
		\ar[d]_\circ
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& {Q}_n \times {Q}_\bullet \ar[d]^\circ \\
	P_{\sum{k_i}} \rtwocell^{\alpha_{\sum{k_i}}}_{\beta_{\sum{k_i}}}
		{*{!(-3.5,0)\object{\eta_{\sum{k_i}}}}}
	& Q_{\sum{k_i}}
} \\
(\eta_1)_{1} &= &1 \\
\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	P_n \rtwocell^{\alpha_n}_{\beta_n}{*{!(-1,0)\object{\eta_n}}}
		\ar[d]_{\sigma\cdot-}
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& Q_n \ar[d]^{\sigma\cdot-} \\
	P_n \ar[r]_{\beta_n} & Q_n
}
&
	        \xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
		\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
		\xymatrix{ {} \ar @{}[d]^{=} \\ {} }

&\xymatrixrowsep{4pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{4pc}
\xymatrix{
	P_n \ar[r]^{\alpha_n}
		\ar[d]_{\sigma\cdot-}
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& Q_n \ar[d]^{\sigma\cdot-} \\
	P_n \rtwocell^{\alpha_n}_{\beta_n}{*{!(-1,0)\object{\eta_n}}} & Q_n
}
\end{eqnarray}}
hold, for all $n, k_1 \dots k_n \in \natural$ and every $\sigma \in S_n$.
As above, it is enough to show that the images of both sides under $\gamma$
are equal, and this is trivially true by definition of $\eta$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{thm:pres_indep}
\index{presentation!independence of weakenings}
Let $\Phi \in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^\natural$ and let $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \to P$ be a regular epi.
Then ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}$ is equivalent as a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad to {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}.
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Let $Q$ be the weakening of $P$ with respect to $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \to P$.
By the triangle identities, we have a commutative square
\[
\xymatrix{
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[r]^\phi \ar[d]_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \overline\phi}
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^{\epsilon_P}
	& P
}
\]
By functoriality of the factorization system, this gives rise to a unique map
$\chi: Q \to {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$ such that 
\[
\xymatrix{
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/u0.7cm/[rr]^\phi \ar[d]_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \overline\phi}
	& Q \ar@{(>->}[r] \ar@{..>}[d]^\chi
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/d0.7cm/[rr]_{\epsilon_P}
	& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}} \ar@{(>->}[r]
	& P
}
\]
commutes.
We wish to find a pseudo-inverse to $\chi$.

Since \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}\ is monadic over $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^\natural$, a regular epi in
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{$\Sigma$-Operad}}}}\ is a levelwise surjection by Theorem
\ref{thm:reg epis split in Set^X^T}.
So we may choose a section $\psi_n$ of $\phi_n : ({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi)_n \to P_n$ for
all $n \in \natural$.
So we have a morphism $\psi : {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \to {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi$ in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^\natural$.
We wish to show that
\[
\xymatrix{
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^{\epsilon_P} \ar[d]_{\overline\psi}
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[r]^\phi
	& P
}
\]
commutes.
This follows from a simple transpose argument:
\[
\newdir{((}{{}*!/-5pt/{}}
\xymatrixrowsep{0.15pc}
\xymatrix{
& {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^{\bar \psi} & {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[r]^\phi & P \\
\ar@{((-((}[rrrr] & & & & \\
& {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^\psi & {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar[r]^{{\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} \phi} & {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P & =
& {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^1 & {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \\
& & & & \ar@{-}[rrr] & & & \\
& & & & & {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar[r]^\epsilon & P.
}
\]
This induces a map
\[
\xymatrix{
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}}} P \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/u0.7cm/[rr]^{\epsilon_P}
		\ar[d]_{\overline\psi}
	& {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}} \ar@{(>->}[r] \ar@{..>}[d]^\omega
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}} \Phi \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/d0.7cm/[rr]_\phi
	& Q \ar@{(>->}[r]
	& P
}
\]
We will show that $\omega$ is pseudo-inverse to $\chi$.
Now,
\[
\xymatrix{
	Q \ar@{(>->}[r] \ar[d]_\omega
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}} \ar@{(>->}[r] \ar[d]_\chi
	& P \ar[d]^1 \\
	Q \ar@{(>->}[r]
	& P
}
\]
commutes.
So $\xymatrix{Q\ar@<0.5ex>[r]^-{1_Q} \ar@<-0.5ex>[r]_-{\chi\omega} & Q \ar@{(>->}[r] & P}$ is a fork.
By Lemma \ref{lem:fork}, $\chi\omega \cong 1_Q$, and similarly $\omega\chi
\cong 1_{{\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}}$.
So $Q \simeq {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$ as a symmetric \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operad, as required.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:unbiased_symm}
\index{unbiased!weakening of a plain operad!comparison to symmetric weakening}
Let $P$ be a plain operad.
Then ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}) \simeq {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk(${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$)}}}$.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Let $\phi: {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}} P \to P$ be the component at $P$ of the counit of the
adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\rm pl}}}$.
Let $\epsilon$ be the counit of the adjunction ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \dashv {\ensuremath{U^{\Sigma}_{\rm pl}}}$.

By Theorem \ref{thm:plain_as_symmetric}, there is an isomorphism ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}}
({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{\phi}(P)$}}}) \cong {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}}$, and by Theorem
\ref{thm:pres_indep}, there is an equivalence ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk$_{{\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} \phi}({\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P)$}}}
\simeq {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk(${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$)}}}$.
Hence ${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} ({\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}) \simeq {\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk(${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$)}}}$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a plain operad.
Then the category \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-$P$-Cat}}}}\ is equivalent to the category
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Wk-${\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}^{\rm pl}}} P$-Cat}}}}.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- example-35: body_md -->
\index{sets}
Considering again the trivial theory $0$, we see that $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Triv}}}} \simeq \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$.
<!-- end example-35 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a set, and $f$ be a regular epi in the category $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Multicat}}}}_X$ or
in the category $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-$\Sigma$-Multicat}}}}_X$.
Then $f$ is locally surjective on objects.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X$ is monadic over $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multigraph}}}}_X$ by Lemma
\ref{lem:frees_exist} and Theorem \ref{lem:monadj}, and an object of
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multigraph}}}}_X$ can be considered as an object of $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}^Y$, where $Y
= X \times X^*$, and $X^*$ is the free monoid on $X$: for each $x \in X$, and
each sequence $x_1, \dots, x_n \in X^*$, there is a set of funnels $x_1, \dots,
x_n \to x$.
Hence, by \ref{thm:reg epis split in Set^X^T}, every regular epi in
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X$ is locally surjective.

The objects functor $O: \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}$ has both a left adjoint $D$
and a right adjoint $I$.
Hence $O$ and $I$ preserve products, and hence by Lemma \ref{lem:frees_exist}
they induce an adjunction
\[
                           
	\xymatrix{
		\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Multicat}}}}_X \ar@<1ex>[r]^-{O_*}_-{\bot}
		& \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Multicat}}}}_X \ar@<1.1ex>[l]^-{I_*}
	}
.
\]
Since $O_*$ is a left adjoint, it preserves colimits, and in particular regular
epis: hence, every regular epi in $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Multicat}}}}_X$ must be locally surjective
on objects.

The symmetric case is proved analogously.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a (symmetric) multicategory, and $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\rm pl}}}\Phi \to M$
(or in the symmetric case, $\phi : {\ensuremath{F_{\Sigma}}}\Phi \to M$) be a regular epi.
Then the weakening of $M$ with respect to $\phi$ is equivalent as a
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-multicategory to ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($M$)}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
The proof is exactly as for Theorem \ref{thm:pres_indep}.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- defn-92: body_md -->
\index{2-monad}
A \textbf{2-monad} is a monad object in the 2-category of 2-categories, in the
sense of \cite{street}; that is to say, a 2-category $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, a strict 2-functor
$T: \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, and 2-transformations $\mu : T^2 \to T$ and $\eta : 1_\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}} \to T$
satisfying the usual monad laws:
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
	& T^3 \ar[dr]^{\mu T} \ar[dl]_{T \mu} \\
	T^2 \ar[dr]_{\mu} & & T^2 \ar[dl]^\mu \\
	& T
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
	T \ar[r]^{T\eta} \ar[dr]_{1_T}
	& T^2 \ar[d]^\mu
	& T \ar[l]_{\eta T} \ar[dl]^{1_T} \\
	& T
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end defn-92 -->
<!-- defn-93: body_md -->
\index{algebra!for a 2-monad}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, T, \mu, \eta)$ be a 2-monad.
A \textbf{strict algebra} for $T$ is an object $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ and a 1-cell $a : T
A \to A$ satisfying the following axioms:
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
& T^2 A \ar[dr]^{\mu} \ar[dl]_{T a} \\
	T A \ar[dr]_a & & T A \ar[dl]^a \\
	& A
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\xymatrix{
	A \ar[r]^{\eta} \ar[dr]_{1_A}
	& T A \ar[d]^a \\
	& A
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end defn-93 -->
<!-- defn-94: body_md -->
\index{pseudo-algebra!for a 2-monad}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, T, \mu, \eta)$ be a 2-monad.
A \textbf{pseudo-algebra} for $T$ is an object $A \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$, a 1-cell $a: TA
\to A$, and invertible 2-cells
\[
\xymatrixnocompile{
	& T^2 A \ar[dr]^{\mu} \ar[dl]_{T a}
	\ddtwocell\omit{^*{!(0, -0.5)\object{\alpha}}} \\
	T A \ar[dr]_a & & T A \ar[dl]^a \\
	& A
}
\hskip 2cm
\xymatrixnocompile{
	A \ar[r]^{\eta} \ar[dr]_{1_A}
	\drtwocell\omit{^<-1.7>*{!(0.5,0.5)\object{\beta}}}
	& T A \ar[d]^a \\
	& A
}
\]
satisfying the equations
\begin{equation}
\xymatrixnocompile{
& T^3 A \ar[dl]_{T^2 a} \ar[dr]^{\mu T} \ar[dd]^{T \mu}
& & & & T^3 A \ar[dl]_{T^2 a} \ar[dr]^{\mu T}  \ddtwocell\omit{=} \\
T^2 A \ar[dd]_{Ta}
& {} \drtwocell\omit{=} & T^2 A \ar[dd]^{\mu}
& & T^2 A \ar[dd]_{Ta} \ar[dr]_{\mu}
& & T^2 A \ar[dd]^{\mu} \ar[dl]^{Ta} \\
\urtwocell\omit{*{!(-1, -1.5)\object{T \alpha}}}
& T^2 A \ar[dl]_{T a} \ar[dr]_{\mu}
& {} & = 
& & T A \ar[dd]^a
& \\                                 
T A \ar[dr]_a
& & T A \ar[dl]^a
& & T A \ar[dr]_a
& \ultwocell\omit{\alpha} \urtwocell\omit{\alpha}
& T A \ar[dl]^a \\
& A \uutwocell\omit{\alpha}
& & & & A
}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
                                                                         
                     
\xymatrix{
& T A \ar@/u0.8cm/[ddl]_1 \ar@/u0.8cm/[ddr]^1 \ar[d]|{T \eta}
& & & TA \ar@/l0.5cm/[dd]_a \ar@/r0.5cm/[dd]^a \ddtwocell\omit{=}
& & & TA \ar[dl]_a \ar@/ur1cm/[ddrr]^1 \ar[dr]^{\eta T}  \ddtwocell\omit{=} \\
& T^2 A \ar[dl]_{T a} \ar[dr]^\mu 
& & =
& & =
& A \ar[dr]^\eta \ar@/dl1cm/[ddrr]_1
  \drlowertwocell\omit{^<1.7>*{!(-0.5,-0.5)\object{\beta}}}
& & T^2 A \ar[dr]^\mu \ar[dl]_{T a}\\
TA \ar[dr]_a
& & TA \ar[dl]^a
& & A
& & & TA \ar[dr]_a
& & TA \ar[dl]^a\\
& A \uutwocell\omit{\alpha}
& & & & & & & A \uutwocell\omit{\alpha}
}
\end{equation}
<!-- end defn-94 -->
<!-- defn-95: body_md -->
\index{pseudo-algebra!for a 2-monad!pseudo-morphisms}
Let $(\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}, T, \mu, \eta)$ be a 2-monad, and let $(A, a, \alpha_1, \alpha_2)$ and
$(B, b, \beta_1, \beta_2)$ be pseudo-algebras for $T$.
A \textbf{pseudo-morphism of pseudo-algebras} $(A, a, \alpha_1, \alpha_2)$ to
$(B, b, \beta_1, \beta_2)$ is a pair $(f, \phi)$, where $f : A \to B$ is a
1-cell in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$ and $\phi$ is an invertible 2-cell:
\[
\xymatrix{
TA \ar[r]^{Tf} \ar[d]_a \drtwocell\omit{\phi}
& TB \ar[d]^b \\
A \ar[r]_f & B
}
\]
satisfying the axioms
\begin{eqnarray}
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	T^2 A \ar[r]^{T^2 f} \ar[d]_{\mu_A}\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& T^2 B \ar[d]^{\mu_B} \\
	T A \ar[r]^{Tf} \ar[d]_a \drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& T B \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar[r]_f
	& B
}
\xymatrix{ {} \\ = }
\xymatrix{
	T^2 A \ar[r]^{T^2 f} \ar[d]_{T a}
	\drtwocell\omit{*{!(-2,0)\object{T \phi}}}
	& T^2 B \ar[d]^{T b} \\
	T A \ar[r]^{Tf} \ar[d]_a \drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& T B \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar[r]_f
	& B
}
\\
\xymatrixrowsep{3pc}
\xymatrixcolsep{3pc}
\xymatrix{
	A \ar[r]^f \ar[d]_{\eta_A}
		\ddlowertwocell<-13>_{1_A}{*{!(0,1)\object{\alpha_2^{-1}}}}
		\drtwocell\omit{=}
	& B \ar[d]^{\eta_B}
		\dduppertwocell<13>^{1_B}{*{!(0,1)\object{\beta_2^{-1}}}} \\
	T A \ar[r]^{T f} \ar[d]_a \drtwocell\omit{\phi}
	& T B \ar[d]^b \\
	A \ar[r]_f
	& B
}
\xymatrix{ {} \\ = }
\xymatrix{
	\\
	A \rtwocell^f_f{*{!(-0.5,0)\object{1_f}}} & B
}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-95 -->
<!-- theorem-26: body_md -->
(Blackwell, Kelly, Power)
\label{thm:ps-classifier}
Let $T$ be a 2-monad with rank on a cocomplete 2-category $K$, let $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm str}$
be the 2-category of strict $T$-algebras and strict morphisms, and $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm wk}$
be the 2-category of strict $T$-algebras and weak morphisms.
Then the inclusion $J : \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm str} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm wk}$ has a left adjoint $L$.
Thus every strict $T$-algebra $A$ has a \textbf{pseudo-morphism classifier} $p
: A \to A'$ (where $A' = JLA$), such that for all $B \in K$, and every
pseudo-morphism $f: A \to B$, we may express $f$ uniquely as the composite of
$p$ and a strict morphism:
\[
\xymatrix{
	A \ar[r]^p \ar[dr]_f & A' \ar@{..>}[d]^{J\bar f} \\ & B
}
\]
<!-- end theorem-26 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
See \cite{bkp}, Theorem 3.13.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- theorem-27: body_md -->
(Blackwell, Kelly, Power)
\label{thm:f* adj}
Let $f:S \to T$ be a strict map between 2-monads with rank on a cocomplete
2-category $K$.
Then the induced map $f^* : \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm str} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(S)$}}}}_{\rm str}$ has a left adjoint, and 
the induced map $f^* : \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm wk} \to \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(S)$}}}}_{\rm wk}$ has a left biadjoint.
<!-- end theorem-27 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
See \cite{bkp}, Theorem 5.12.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:ps-alg adj}
Composing this left adjoint with the left adjoint of Theorem
\ref{thm:ps-classifier} gives us an adjunction
\[
\NoCompileMatrices
                           
	\xymatrix{
		\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(S)$}}}}_{\rm wk} \ar@<1ex>[r]^-{F}_-{\bot}
		& \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$(T)$}}}}_{\rm str} \ar@<1.1ex>[l]^-{U}
	}

\]
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- theorem-28: body_md -->
(Power, Lack)
\label{thm:ps-classifier as boff}
Let $T$ be a 2-monad with rank on a cocomplete 2-category $K$ of the form
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^X$ for some set $X$, and let $T$ preserve pointwise
bijectivity-on-objects.
Let $(A, a)$ be a strict $T$-algebra.
Then the pseudo-morphism classifier $A'$ for $A$ may be found by factorizing the
structure map $a : TA \to A$ as a pointwise bijective-on-objects map followed
by a locally full-and-faithful map:
\[
\xymatrix{
	TA \ar[rr]^a \ar@{->>}[dr] & & A \\ & A' \ar@{(>->}[ur]
}
\]
<!-- end theorem-28 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
The construction is given in Power's paper \cite{power}, and the universal
property of the algebra constructed is proved in Lack's paper \cite{lack}.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- theorem-29: body_md -->
\label{thm:ps-algs are weak algs}
Let $P$ be a plain operad.
Let $T_P$ be the monad induced by $P$ on \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Set}}}}.
Then a pseudo-algebra for $\bar T_P$ is a weak $P$-category in the sense of
Definition \ref{def:weakening}.
Furthermore, there is an isomorphism of categories $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Ps-Alg$(\bar T_P)$}}}} \cong
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Alg$_{\rm wk}(P)$}}}}$.
<!-- end theorem-29 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat-Operad}}}}\ is monadic over $\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}^\natural$ via one of the special monads of
Theorem \ref{thm:ps-classifier as boff}, and hence, for every plain
$\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}$-operad $P$, the pseudo-morphism classifier of $P$ is none other than
${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}}$.
Hence, if $A$ is a category, then a strict map of \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}-operads ${\ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape Wk($P$)}}} \to
\mathop{\rm{End}}(A)$ is precisely a weak map $P \to \mathop{\rm{End}}(A)$, or equivalently a
$\bar T_P$-pseudo-algebra structure on $A$.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- theorem-30: body_md -->
\index{commutative monoids}
A pseudo-algebra for $T'$ is a symmetric monoidal category $A$ in which $x
\otimes y = y \otimes x$ for all $x, y \in A$.
<!-- end theorem-30 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
Recall our construction of the finite product operad\ whose algebras are commutative monoids in
Example \ref{ex:comm_monoid_fp}.
From this, we may deduce that if $A$ is a set, then an element of $T_P A$ is a
function $A \to \natural$ assigning each element of $A$ its multiplicity: in
other words, a multiset of elements of $A$.
Let $(A, a, \alpha, \beta)$ be a pseudo-algebra for $T'$ in \ensuremath{\mbox{\upshape{\textbf{Cat}}}}.
Then we have a binary tensor product:
\[
x\otimes y := a(x^1y^1)
\]
where $x^1y^1$ is the function $A \to \natural$ sending $x$ and $y$ to 1 and
all other objects of $A$ to 0.
The tensor is defined analogously on morphisms.
The components of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ give us associator, symmetry and unit
maps, and it can be shown that they satisfy the axioms for a monoidal category.
However, since the function $x^1y^1$ is equal to the function $y^1x^1$ for all
$x, y \in A$, it must be the case that $x \otimes y = y \otimes x$.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- defn-96: body_md -->
\index{Laplaza set}
Let $T$ be a finite product operad.
A \textbf{Laplaza set} for $T$ is a subsignature of ${\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} T$.
<!-- end defn-96 -->
<!-- defn-97: body_md -->
\index{pseudo-algebra!for a finite product operad\ with Laplaza set}
Let $T$ be a finite product operad, and $S$ be a Laplaza set for $T$.
A \textbf{$(T,S)$-pseudo algebra} is
\begin{itemize}
\item a category \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}\,
\item for each $\phi \in T_n$, a functor $\hat \phi : \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}^n \to \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}$,
\item \textbf{coherence morphisms} witnessing all equations that are true in
$T$,
\end{itemize}
such that, if
\begin{itemize}
\item $s_1, s_2, t_1$ and $t_2$ are elements of $({\ensuremath{F_{\rm fp}}}{\ensuremath{U^{\rm fp}}} T)_n$,
\item $\delta_1: \hat s_1 \to \hat t_1$ and $\delta_2: \hat s_2 \to \hat t_2$
are coherence morphisms,
\item $\epsilon(s_1) = \epsilon(s_2) \in S$ and $\epsilon(t_1) = \epsilon(t_2)
\in S$,
\end{itemize}
then $\delta_1 = \delta_2$.
<!-- end defn-97 -->
